## 65. Explain SAP FICO Architect Library — Asset Accounting complete: HGB vs IFRS vs Turkish (VUK/TFRS) - configuration to financial statements.md — the key SAP FICO content, configuration and numbers I should know from this resource

### 🗣️ DIRECT ANSWER TO SPEAK NOW
- **Core Concept:** Same data, different rules: HGB is conservative and tax-linked for the German statutory books, IFRS is decision-useful for investors, and Turkish reporting splits into VUK (tax procedure law and uniform chart of accounts, tax-driven) and TMS/TFRS (IFRS-adapted financial reporting under KGK). In S/4HANA one transaction posts once and the ledgers carry the differences: 0L IFRS, L1 HGB, L2 VUK, L3 TFRS.
- HGB: German Commercial Code, focus on creditor protection and prudence, generally conservative, used for statutory financial statements, may differ from German tax law (EStG).
- IFRS: international standards for comparable, decision-useful information for listed groups; fair value where relevant, more principle-based and flexible.
- Turkish: VUK is the tax procedure law with the uniform chart of accounts (often tax-based, local rules apply, TMS/TFRS may differ), while TMS/TFRS is the IFRS-adapted framework from KGK and BOBI FRS for local statutory and tax compliance.

### ⚖️ SIDE-BY-SIDE — HGB (GERMANY) vs IFRS AND TURKISH (VUK / TMS-TFRS)
| Dimension | HGB (Germany) | IFRS and Turkish (VUK / TMS-TFRS) | What I do in SAP |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Primary purpose | Statutory accounts, creditor protection | IFRS: reporting for investors. Turkish: VUK local statutory/tax compliance; TFRS financial reporting | Parallel ledgers in FINSC_LEDGER: 0L IFRS, L1 HGB, L2 VUK, L3 TFRS on one company code set |
| Asset valuation | Historical cost, conservative | IFRS: historical cost or fair value (depends). VUK: often tax-based cost, local rules; depreciation keys differ by law | Depreciation areas per principle (OADB 01/10/15/30-32) with their own keys and useful lives |
| Depreciation | Based on HGB rules | IFRS: based on useful life and components. VUK (from the CYBEX-Adesso TR email): straight-line STR, declining-balance DBL at straight-line rate x2 (max 50%), pro-rata Kist Amortisman, extraordinary Fevkalade as unplanned posting | Depreciation key per area: base method, multilevel method, period control; AFAB runs per area |
| Provisions | Only certain provisions (HGB section 249) | IFRS: IAS 37 present obligation. Turkish: depends on framework; tax deductibility under VUK is not automatic | Same accrual document, recognition per ledger; never average the principles |
| Revenue | Realisation and accrual principles | IFRS: IFRS 15 five-step model. Turkish: local rules may differ from IFRS 15 | Billing posts once (VF01); the reporting difference is read per ledger |
| Leases and deferred tax | Different treatment (not IFRS 16); HGB-specific deferred tax rules | IFRS: IFRS 16 ROU asset and lease liability; IAS 12 temporary differences. Turkish: depends on VUK or TMS; separate tax reporting, local rules; TMS 29 inflation applies in Turkey when criteria are met | Ledger-specific postings (FBB1 with ledger group); TMS 29 restatement handled per Turkish requirements |
| Output | Statutory financial statements | IFRS: consolidated reporting (often for listed companies). Turkish: requirements defined by KGK and Turkish regulations | F.01 per ledger from the same ACDOCA data; each principle reconciles on its own |

### 🗣️ DIRECT ANSWER TO SPEAK NOW
- **Core Concept:** Asset Accounting end to end: a business transaction (PO, invoice, retirement) hits the asset master (AS01), posts into the General Ledger (ACDOCA), is valued per ledger (0L IFRS, L1 HGB, L2 VUK, L3 TFRS), and reports in F.01/F.07 per ledger up to Group Consolidation. The same transaction gives different results under HGB, IFRS and Turkish rules: asset class plus transaction type plus account modifier derives the G/L account in AO90, the G/L comes from the operating chart of accounts, and in FS00 almost all asset master G/Ls (APC, accumulated depreciation, special reserve) are balance sheet accounts; the P&L exceptions are depreciation expense, impairment loss, gain/loss on sale, retirement loss and scrap loss.
- **Key System Benefit:** One integrated process with one correct posting per ledger: correct configuration ensures automatic and consistent posting, F.01, ACDOCA and the asset reports show the final values per accounting principle, and nobody maintains parallel asset spreadsheets per GAAP.
- **Execution Strategy:** Configuration chain in key t-codes: EC08 chart of depreciation (copy/create, for example CDDE), OADB depreciation areas (01, 10, 15, 30, 32, 34), OAYZ assign chart of depreciation to company code, AO01 asset classes (number range, description), AO90 account determination (map G/L accounts per class and transaction), OADB depreciation keys (methods, useful life, posting logic), AJRW/AJAB open asset year and posting periods, then the IMG additional settings (transfer of APC values between areas, account modifiers, notes). Prove with the lifecycle: AS01 create, F-90/MIRO acquire, AFAB depreciate, ABUMN transfer and settle, F-92/ABAVN retire or scrap, FAGLLGVTR year-end close, F.01/F.07 report.
- **Scenario Figures I Will Use:** RS1. I keep the same figures through the posting, clearing and test steps; if a rate or account is not given, I state it as an explicit assumption rather than inventing a project value.
- **Objects Detected In The Question/Image:** FAGLL03H, ACDOCA, GURU99, SAPUI5, PH01, OX02, OB13, NI01, PH15, OB53, DE02, CC01, IFRS1.

- **Core Concept:** CO-PA answers which customer, product, country or channel makes money. KE24 shows lines only because the profitability set-up exists: operating concern (KEA0) plus assignment to the controlling area (KEKK) plus activation (KEKE, status 4 = both types). Billing then writes a CO-PA document; KE24 only reads it, and KEBD picks the view. KE4I and KE4M turn SD conditions into costing-based value fields; account-based needs no mapping because the G/L account is the value.
- **Key System Benefit:** One billing creates both views at CYBEX (live as operating concern GB01, combined): account-based margin analysis reads the P&L lines in ACDOCA so it always reconciles to FI, while costing-based reads value fields built from SD conditions for the commercial view.
- **Execution Strategy:** Build order: KEA0 characteristics and value fields, KEKK assignment, KEBD view, KE4I/KE4M condition mapping, KE12/KEU1 transfers, KEKE activation, then KER1/KE31 reporting. Prove it with one billing: VF03, Accounting overview, then KE24 in both views. A posting made before activation will never appear, so activation sequence is a cutover step, not an afterthought.

### 📊 ARCHITECTURAL FLOW
```text
1. SALES ORDER VA01
 no FI posting; pricing runs, profitability segment derived on the item
 ↓
2. GOODS ISSUE VL02N
 Dr COGS 150.00 / Cr Inventory 150.00
 ↓
3. BILLING F2 VF01
 Dr Customer 352.44, Dr Discounts 50.23, Cr Sales 346.40, Cr Output tax 56.27; CO-PA document written because KEA0 + KEKK + KEKE are set
 ↓
4. KE24 ACCOUNT-BASED KE24
 reads the P&L lines of the postings (ACDOCA); the G/L account is the value
 ↓
5. KE24 COSTING-BASED KE24
 reads characteristics + value fields; list price, discounts, net sales, COGS, margin
```

### ⚙️ CONFIG STEPS
1. **KEA0** — define the operating concern: characteristics (the tags: REGIO, LAND1, customer, product) and value fields (ABSMG quantity, ERLOS revenue, VV001 COGS) · Example: Demo system concern 1102 on controlling area 2018; CYBEX runs the same mechanism live as GB01 (combined account-based + costing-based) · Ref: Profitability Analysis in SAP guide, steps 1-15; SPRO ▸ Controlling ▸ Profitability Analysis.
2. **KEKK** — assign the controlling area to the operating concern · Example: Controlling area 2018 gets operating concern 1102; without this, billing cannot write to CO-PA · Ref: CO-PA guide step 2; SPRO ▸ Controlling ▸ Profitability Analysis ▸ Structures.
3. **KEBD** — set the operating concern and choose the costing-based working mode that KE24 will display · Example: Enter 1102 and pick costing-based to see value fields; switch view to margin analysis for account-based · Ref: CO-PA guide step 3.
4. **KE4I** — assign SD condition types to CO-PA value fields (condition to ERLOS or VV001) - costing-based values come from here · Example: Z001 list price, Z312 promo discount, Z205 general discount and VPRS cost mapped to their own value fields; a new condition type needs a value field, activation and regeneration of the operating concern · Ref: CO-PA guide step 4 (poster shows KEAI/KE4I spelling variants from OCR; the transaction is KE4I).
5. **KE4M** — assign quantity fields: SD quantity to ABSMG · Example: One stroller sold writes quantity 1 into ABSMG so KE24 can show volumes beside values · Ref: CO-PA guide step 5; standard transaction KE4M.
6. **KE12** — PA transfer structure for direct FI/MM postings that have no billing behind them · Example: A direct FI posting on cost account 400400 moves into value field KWSMKT; optional, not needed for the billing example · Ref: CO-PA guide step 6.
7. **KEU1** — cost center assessment cycles into CO-PA (cycle ASS110 moves overhead from cost centers) · Example: Optional assessment step; not part of the one-billing example · Ref: CO-PA guide step 7.
8. **KEKE** — activate Profitability Analysis: active status 4 means active for both types · Example: Without KEKE nothing reaches KE24; and a posting made before activation will not appear later · Ref: CO-PA guide step 8.
9. **KER1** — key figure scheme 01: revenue minus COGS equals contribution margin, used by the KE30 report · Example: The margin column in the report is this scheme, not a KE24 line calculation · Ref: CO-PA guide step 9.
10. **KE31** — create the report (Region-wise Profitability: Country, Region, Company code, Fiscal year) for KE30 · Example: Reporting layer only; KE24 line items exist independently of the report · Ref: CO-PA guide step 10.
11. **KE24** — display CO-PA line items and switch between margin analysis (account-based) and costing-based with the radio button · Example: Same sales order, two truths: G/L lines in one view, value fields in the other · Ref: CO-PA guide, example section A and B.

### 🔧 DROP THESE OBJECT NAMES
- **KEA0** — operating concern: characteristics + value fields.
- **KEKK** — assign operating concern to controlling area.
- **KEBD** — set operating concern / pick the KE24 view.
- **KEKE** — activation, status 4 = both types active.
- **KE4I** — SD conditions to value fields (costing-based values).
- **KE4M** — quantity field assignment (ABSMG).
- **KEDR** — derivation of the profitability segment on the sales order item.
- **KE24** — CO-PA line item display.
- **GB01** — CYBEX live combined operating concern.
- **CE1-CE4** — costing-based CO-PA tables in S/4HANA (CE1 to CE4 of the operating concern).

### 🧾 ACCOUNTING ENTRIES
- Goods issue (VL02N): Dr COGS 5111000000 EUR 150.00 / Cr Inventory EUR 150.00 - the PGI line that account-based KE24 shows as COGS 150.00.
- Billing F2 (VF01): Dr Customer EUR 352.44 (incl. VAT), Dr Discounts 4411000000 EUR 50.23 (Z312 promo 5% = 17.32 plus Z205 general 10% = 32.91), Cr Sales 4111000000 EUR 346.40 (Z001 list price), Cr Output tax EUR 56.27 (19% on net 296.17).
- KE24 account-based (margin analysis) for DE02: PGI 5111000000 150.00; F2 billing 4111000000 -346.40; discounts 4411000000 +17.32 and +32.91; Net P&L margin -146.17 (credit). No sales order line, no customer, no VAT, no inventory in this view.
- KE24 costing-based for the same billing: quantity 1, list price 346.40, promo -17.32, general -32.91, net sales 296.17, COGS 150.00, margin 146.17. Net sales check: 346.40 - 17.32 - 32.91 = 296.17; margin: 296.17 - 150.00 = 146.17.

### 🧪 HOW TO TEST IT
1. Prove it in 5 minutes: 1) KEA0 display shows both types ticked. 2) KEKK: controlling area assigned. 3) KEKE: status 4. 4) KE4I: Z001, Z312, Z205, VPRS mapped. 5) VF03 on the billing, Accounting overview: accounting, controlling and profitability documents all exist; then KE24 in both views by sales order.
2. Post the same billing before KEKE activation in a test system and show KE24 stays empty - activation sequence is the lesson.
3. Agree account-based KE24 revenue for one period to FAGLL03H on the same company code, period and ledger 0L; they must tie because both read ACDOCA.
4. Change one SD condition (add a new discount) and show costing-based needs KE4I mapping plus operating-concern regeneration before the value field fills.

## 69. Explain SAP FICO Architect Library — Turkey CTP TR02 Rollout — full intercompany, e-Fatura, FX and tax.md — the key SAP FICO content, configuration and numbers I should know from this resource

### 🗣️ DIRECT ANSWER TO SPEAK NOW
- **Core Concept:** I treat a new company code as a legal reporting entity, not as a copied code. I freeze the local legal, tax, banking and reporting requirements first, copy the closest approved template, localize only what the country changes, integrate the selling/purchasing channels and the advanced intercompany supply between company codes, then prove the first invoice, payment, asset, close and statutory report before cutover. That is the pattern behind my five CYBEX rollouts — Paris, Berlin and New York stores, IMEA and the UK entity.
- **Key System Benefit:** In S/4HANA the company code posts into ACDOCA by ledger and accounting principle, so HGB/local books and IFRS group reporting can be produced from the same document instead of reconciling a second local system at month-end.
- **Execution Strategy:** The build order is enterprise structure, controlling assignment, global parameters, chart of accounts and tax, master data, integration determination, banking, intercompany clearing and billing, cutover balances and period controls — in that order, because every later object inherits the company-code currency, fiscal year and ledger design. Advanced intercompany is designed at rollout time, not bolted on: cross-company stock transfer, OBYA clearing, intercompany billing and FBICR3 reconciliation are part of the template.

### 💡 SAY THIS FIRST

```
 create TR02, local currency TRY, country TR

 ↓

 valuation class 3000, cost element ZCOGS

 ↓

 valuation class 3000 → G/L 5111000000 (custom COGS)

 ↓
5. CUSTOM POSTING PROGRAM ZFI_COGS (PH16)
 called on goods issue via BADI MB_MIGO_GOODSMVT_POST

```

2. **OX15** — create the company code, legal entity with its own books · Example: TR02, TRY, Turkey · Where: SPRO ▸ Enterprise Structure ▸ Definition ▸ Financial Accounting ▸ Edit, Copy, Delete, Check Company Code
3. **SKA1** — create the custom G/L account for COGS · Example: 5111000000, “Custom COGS”, account type S · Where: SPRO ▸ Financial Accounting ▸ General Ledger ▸ Master Data ▸ G/L Accounts ▸ Edit G/L Account Master Data

5. **T042I** — extend cost‑element mapping for custom COGS · Example: ZCOGS → 5111000000 · Where: SPRO ▸ Controlling ▸ Cost Element Accounting ▸ Cost Element → G/L Account Assignment
6. **OBYC** — configure automatic account determination for valuation class 3000 · Example: transaction 40, valuation class 3000 → 5111000000 · Where: SPRO ▸ Materials Management ▸ Valuation and Account Assignment ▸ Account Determination ▸ Configure Automatic Posting
7. **ZFI_COGS** — activate custom posting program (PH16) in enhancement spot BADI MB_MIGO_GOODSMVT_POST · Example: program writes additional line to ACDOCA on goods issue · Where: SE18 ▸ BADI → MB_MIGO_GOODSMVT_POST → Implementation → ZFI_COGS

- **Goods Issue (VL01N / VL02N) for 1 Stroller:**
 - Dr. G/L 5111000000 (Cost of sales / COGS) — EUR 150.00
 - Cr. Inventory / Stock Account — EUR 150.00
- **Billing Document F2 (VF01) for 1 Stroller (Company Code DE02):**
 - Dr. Customer Account — EUR 352.44
 - Dr. G/L 4411000000 (Discounts: Z312 promo 5% = EUR 17.32 + Z205 general 10% = EUR 32.91) — EUR 50.23

### HOW TO TEST IT

## 73. Explain SAP S/4HANA Universal Journal ACDOCA and New Asset Accounting architecture

### 💡 SAY THIS FIRST
Universal Journal combines general ledger, asset accounting, and controlling into one single item table, eliminating reconciliation ledgers.

### 🗣️ DIRECT ANSWER TO SPEAK NOW
- **Core Concept:** ACDOCA stores all line items in a single table with up to ten parallel currencies, instantly satisfying multiple accounting principles like IFRS and local GAAP without batch reconciliation.
- **Key System Benefit:** S/4HANA replaced legacy totals tables like GLT0, BSIS, BSAS, and COEP with the Universal Journal, removing month-end reconciliation bottlenecks between FI and CO.
- **Execution Strategy:** FINSC_LEDGER drives the parallel ledgers and accounting principles, while New Asset Accounting integrates asset classes, depreciation areas, and the technical clearing account for parallel valuations.

### 📊 ARCHITECTURAL FLOW
```
1. STRUCTURE FINSC_LEDGER · OAOB
 define ledger 0L (IFRS) and L1 (local GAAP), assign COD and areas

 ↓

2. MASTER DATA AS01 · KA01
 asset class and cost center master drive real-time derivation

3. TRANSACTION F-90 · FB01
 posting writes directly to ACDOCA with split currency views

4. PERIOD CLOSE AFAB · FINS_FXV
 run depreciation and advanced foreign currency valuation by ledger

5. REPORTING FAGLL03 · SE16H
 verify single source of truth across all financial statements

### ⚙️ CONFIG STEPS
1. **FINSC_LEDGER** — define the leading ledger and parallel non-leading ledgers for multiple accounting principles · Example: Ledger 0L assigned to IFRS and L1 assigned to local GAAP · Where: SPRO ▸ Financial Accounting ▸ Financial Accounting Global Settings ▸ Ledgers ▸ Ledger
2. **OAOB** — assign the chart of depreciation to the company code · Example: COD assigned to company code TR02 for statutory depreciation areas · Where: SPRO ▸ Financial Accounting ▸ Asset Accounting ▸ Organizational Structures
3. **OADB** — review depreciation areas and their ledger assignment · Example: Book depreciation to 0L and tax depreciation to non-leading ledger L1 · Where: SPRO ▸ Financial Accounting ▸ Asset Accounting ▸ Valuation
4. **AO90** — maintain account determination for asset classes and depreciation areas · Example: Acquisition, accumulated depreciation and gain/loss accounts separated by asset class · Where: SPRO ▸ Financial Accounting ▸ Asset Accounting ▸ Integration with General Ledger Accounting
5. **AS01** — create the asset master from the correct asset class · Example: Asset class defaults useful life, depreciation key and account determination before acquisition · Where: SAP GUI ▸ Accounting ▸ Financial Accounting ▸ Fixed Assets ▸ Asset
6. **AFAB** — execute the depreciation run for the period · Example: Planned depreciation posted by depreciation area updating the asset history and ACDOCA · Where: SAP GUI ▸ Fixed Assets ▸ Periodic Processing ▸ Depreciation Run

### 🔧 DROP THESE OBJECT NAMES
- **ACDOCA** — Universal Journal line item table
- **FINSC_LEDGER** — define ledgers and accounting principles
- **OAOB** — assign chart of depreciation
- **OADB** — depreciation area definition
- **AO90** — asset account determination
- **AFAB** — depreciation posting run
- **SE16H** — fast join and reporting table view

### 🧾 ACCOUNTING ENTRIES
- Dr Fixed asset 50,000 / Cr Technical clearing account 50,000 — integrated asset acquisition before area-specific valuation.
- Dr Technical clearing account 50,000 / Cr Vendor 50,000 — vendor liability posting linked to technical clearing.
- Dr Depreciation expense 50,000 / Cr Accumulated depreciation 50,000 — AFAB period-end depreciation run.
- Dr Accumulated depreciation 50,000 / Cr Fixed asset 50,000 — asset retirement removing cost and reserves.

### 🧪 HOW TO TEST IT
1. Open SE16H and inspect table ACDOCA to confirm postings contain ledger, company code, and currency dimensions.
2. Create an asset in AS01, post an acquisition via F-90, and inspect every depreciation area in AW01N.
3. Run depreciation in AFAB in test mode, correct any error, then execute the update run.
4. Verify parallel ledger balances using FAGLL03 to confirm IFRS and local GAAP reports match expectations.

### 🪤 TRAPS & THE ANSWER THAT WINS
- Trap: Assuming classic reconciliation tables still exist in S/4HANA for month-end balance checks. → Winning line: ACDOCA is the single source of truth, making classic reconciliation tables obsolete.
- Trap: Treating parallel asset valuation as requiring duplicate asset masters for each accounting principle. → Winning line: New Asset Accounting uses one asset master with multiple depreciation areas mapped to different ledgers.

### 🎯 IF MY MIND GOES BLANK
ACDOCA is the single table holding all finance and controlling line items, while New Asset Accounting uses technical clearing accounts and depreciation areas to post parallel valuations instantly.
```

```
## 74. Controlling area

### 💡 SAY THIS FIRST
A controlling area groups cost accounting across legal entities so we can analyze profitability consistently.

### 🗣️ DIRECT ANSWER TO SPEAK NOW (speak aloud in ~30-45 secs)
- **Core Concept:** It is the top‑level CO unit that collects all cost and revenue postings for the assigned company codes.
- **Key System Benefit:** In S/4HANA the postings flow directly into ACDOCA, eliminating the CO‑FI reconciliation tables (COEP/COBK) used in ECC.
- **Execution Strategy:** Create the controlling area (OKKP), assign company codes (OX06), define primary cost elements (KA06) and cost centers (KS01), then set up automatic account determination (OBYC) with the proper access sequence.

### 📊 ARCHITECTURAL FLOW
```
1. CONTROLLING AREA OKKP · OX06
 define GB01, currency EUR, FYV K4, version 0
 assign company code TR02

 ↓
2. PRIMARY COST ELEMENT KA06
 400000 “Material Expenses” → GL 600000
 category 1, auto‑create from GL

 ↓
3. COST CENTER KS01
 2000 “Production”, hierarchy H01
 responsible John Doe

 ↓
4. MANUAL COST POSTING KB11N
 Dr 400000 / Cr 2000 10 000 TRY – when posting
```

### ⚙️ CONFIG STEPS
1. **OKKP** — create the controlling area, top CO unit · Example: GB01, currency EUR, FYV K4, version 0 · Where: SPRO ▸ Controlling ▸ General Controlling ▸ Maintain Controlling Area
 2. **OX06** — assign company code to the controlling area · Example: TR02 → GB01 · Where: SPRO ▸ Enterprise Structure ▸ Assignment ▸ Financial Accounting ▸ Assign Company Code to Controlling Area
 3. **KA06** — define primary cost element (expense) · Example: 400000 “Material Expenses” linked to GL 600000 · Where: SPRO ▸ Controlling ▸ Cost Element Accounting ▸ Primary Cost Elements
 4. **OKA1** — enable auto‑creation of primary cost elements from GL accounts · Example: auto‑create 400000 from GL 600000 · Where: SPRO ▸ Controlling ▸ Cost Element Accounting ▸ Automatic Creation
 5. **KS01** — create cost center master data · Example: 2000 “Production”, hierarchy H01, responsible John Doe · Where: SPRO ▸ Controlling ▸ Cost Center Accounting ▸ Master Data ▸ Cost Center
 6. **OBYC** — set automatic account determination for cost‑element postings · Example: transaction key “K” → GL 600000 (expense) · Where: SPRO ▸ Financial Accounting ▸ Global Settings ▸ Document → Posting → Automatic Account Determination
 7. **KB11N** — test manual cost posting in CO · Example: post 10 000 TRY to cost element 400000, cost center 2000 · Where: SAP Easy Access ▸ Accounting ▸ Controlling ▸ Cost Element Accounting ▸ Manual Posting

### 🔧 DROP THESE OBJECT NAMES
- **OKKP** — controlling‑area definition, top CO hierarchy
- **OX06** — company‑code to controlling‑area assignment
- **KA06** — primary cost‑element creation, links to GL
- **KS01** — cost‑center master record, hierarchy node
- **OBYC** — automatic GL‑account determination for CO postings
- **KB11N** — manual CO posting transaction, test driver

### 🧾 ACCOUNTING ENTRIES
Dr 400000 (Primary Expense) 10 000 TRY / Cr 2000 (Cost Center) 10 000 TRY — when KB11N posts the cost

### 🧪 HOW TO TEST IT
1. Execute **KB11N**, enter cost element 400000, cost center 2000, amount 10 000 TRY, post.
2. Open **FBL3N**, display GL 600000, verify the debit of 10 000 TRY.
3. Run **S_ALR_87013611** (Cost Center Actual/Plan) for cost center 2000, confirm the expense line.
4. Use **SE16H** on table **ACDOCA**, filter KOSTL = 2000 and KSTAR = 400000, check the line item.

### 🪤 TRAPS & THE ANSWER THAT WINS
- Trap: “One controlling area can only serve one company code.” → Winning line: “A controlling area can cover many company codes; we linked TR02 to GB01.”
- Trap: “Currency must match the company‑code currency.” → Winning line: “The controlling‑area currency is for CO reporting only; postings are converted to the company‑code currency at posting time.”

DIRECT ANSWER TO SPEAK NOW
The controlling area (`KOKRS`) is the central organizational umbrella for internal accounting, covering cost centers, profit centers, internal orders, and profitability analysis (`CO-PA`). One controlling area can span multiple company codes—such as our global setup where controlling area `GBGR` covers 27 company codes, or specific regional rollouts like CTP Turkey (`TR02` posting period variant context). The mandatory technical prerequisite for assigning multiple company codes to a single controlling area is that they must share the identical operational Chart of Accounts and Fiscal Year Variant.

ARCHITECTURAL FLOW
```
[Controlling Area: KOKRS (e.g., GBGR covering 27 CoCodes)]
 |
 +---> [Company Code 1: DE02 (Shared CoA + Fiscal Year Variant)]
 |
 +---> [Company Code 2: GB01 (Shared CoA + Fiscal Year Variant)]
 |
 +---> [Company Code N: TR02 / CTP Turkey (Shared CoA + Fiscal Year Variant)]
 |
 v
[Universal Journal ACDOCA / CO-PA: Real-time integration and cross-company cost allocations]
```

CONFIG STEPS
1. `OKKP` - Define Controlling Area (maintain name, currency type, currency, fiscal year variant, and cost center standard hierarchy).
2. `OX06` - Assign Company Code to Controlling Area (enforces 1:1 or 1:n relationship under strict prerequisite rules).
3. `OKEON` - Cost Center Standard Hierarchy (build and maintain the organizational structure, keeping levels to a maximum of 5 for S/4HANA performance optimization).
4. `KS01` - Create Cost Center (master data creation within the assigned controlling area and hierarchy node).
5. `KA06` / `OKA1` - Cost Element Management (Primary cost elements auto-created via `OKA1` from G/L, Secondary cost elements created manually via `KA06` for internal allocations).
6. `OKB9` - Automatic Account Assignment (default cost center or profitability segment derivation for FI postings without explicit CO objects).

DROP THESE OBJECT NAMES
- OKKS / OX18 (Incorrect assignments; company codes are assigned to controlling areas via `OX06` and maintained in `OKKP`).

ACCOUNTING ENTRIES (WITH NUMBERS)
- Cross-Company Cost Allocation (e.g., assessing internal IT overhead costs of 1,000 TRY from Sender Cost Center 100 in Company Code A to Receiver Cost Center 200 in Company Code B within controlling area `GBGR`):
 - Sender CO Line Item: Dr Receiver Cost Center 200 (CC B) 1,000 TRY / Cr Sender Cost Center 100 (CC A) 1,000 TRY (Generated via secondary cost element category 42 via `KSV5` / assessment).
 - FI Clearing Entry (if cross-company posting): Dr Intercompany Receivable Company Code A 1,000 TRY / Cr Intercompany Payable Company Code B 1,000 TRY, automatically balanced through clearing accounts configured in `OBYA`.

HOW TO TEST IT
1. Verify controlling area configuration using `SE16N` on table `TKA01` (`KOKRS=GBGR`) to inspect assigned company codes and currency settings.
2. Execute transaction `OKKP` to validate that the assigned company codes share the exact same operational Chart of Accounts and Fiscal Year Variant.
3. Post a manual cost allocation using `KB11N` or run an assessment cycle (`KSV5`) across two company codes assigned to the same controlling area and confirm the posting updates table `ACDOCA` in real-time.

TRAPS
- Assuming company codes with different operational Charts of Accounts can be grouped into a single controlling area—they cannot; they require separate controlling areas or a corporate Chart of Accounts harmonization project.
- Forgetting that S/4HANA profit center reporting (`KEF2` / `ACDOCA`) replaces old EC-PCA structures, meaning profit center derivation must be verified globally across the entire controlling area via `1KE5` and `KE5T`.

IF MY MIND GOES BLANK
"The controlling area is my management accounting perimeter. If I span multiple company codes under one controlling area—like `GBGR` covering 27 entities—they must share the same operational chart of accounts and fiscal year variant, allowing me to run cross-company allocations and global profitability reporting clean in `ACDOCA`."

### 🎯 IF MY MIND GOES BLANK
- Controlling area = CO umbrella for cost/revenue.
- Replaces separate CO‑FI reconciliation tables (COEP/COBK).
- Key object: **OKKP**.

## 75. Conditions types

### 💡 SAY THIS FIRST
Condition types are the building blocks in SAP pricing procedures that drive base prices, discounts, freight, and taxes.

### 🗣️ DIRECT ANSWER TO SPEAK NOW
“Condition types drive pricing, discounts, taxes, and surcharges across SD and MM modules in S/4HANA. In SD, pricing procedures like `ZGBE01` control the sequence where conditions like `PR00` (Base Price), `K007` (Customer Discount), `MWST` (Output Tax), and `FRA1` (Freight) calculate values before posting to revenue and subledgers via account determination (`VKOA`/`OBYC`). In MM, procurement condition types like `PB00` (Net Price) and `FRA1` (Freight) govern purchase orders via info records (`ME11`) and pricing procedures (`OMUM`/`OMQ2`), remaining unposted until logistics invoice verification (`MIRO`) generates the FI document.”

### 📊 ARCHITECTURAL FLOW
```
1. CONDITION TYPE V/08 · V/07
 define condition types (PR00, K004, FRA1)
 assign access sequences and calculation types

 ↓

2. PRICING PROCEDURE OMUM · V/08
 group condition types into pricing procedures
 determine step sequence and subtotals

3. CONDITION RECORDS VK11 · ME11
 maintain values for customers or materials
 store condition records with validity dates

4. POSTING TO FI VKOA · OBYC
 transfer condition values to accounting
 map account keys to general ledger accounts

### ⚙️ CONFIG STEPS
1. **V/06** — define condition types specifying calculation type, condition class, and manual entry flags · Example: PR00 base price, calculation type B (quantity/percentage) · Where: SPRO ▸ Sales and Distribution ▸ Basic Functions ▸ Pricing ▸ Pricing Control ▸ Define Condition Types
2. **V/07** — define access sequences to control the search strategy for condition records · Example: Access sequence PR00 searching customer/material then material · Where: SPRO ▸ Sales and Distribution ▸ Basic Functions ▸ Pricing ▸ Pricing Control ▸ Define Access Sequences
3. **V/08** — define pricing procedures by sequencing condition types and specifying requirements · Example: Pricing procedure ZGBEO1 for CTP Turkey with steps for PR00, discounts, and taxes · Where: SPRO ▸ Sales and Distribution ▸ Basic Functions ▸ Pricing ▸ Pricing Control ▸ Define And Assign Pricing Procedures
4. **VK11** — create condition records for pricing elements with specific validity dates and values · Example: Set PR00 to 1,000 TRY for material 520001 and customer KUNNR · Where: Logistics ▸ Sales and Distribution ▸ Master Data ▸ Conditions ▸ Select Using Condition Table
5. **VKOA** — assign general ledger accounts to SD account determination keys for revenue posting · Example: Account key ERL mapped to G/L account 400000 for domestic sales revenue · Where: SPRO ▸ Sales and Distribution ▸ Basic Functions ▸ Pricing ▸ Pricing Determination ▸ Assign Revenue Accounts

### 📦 DROP THESE OBJECT NAMES
- **KE12** — CO-PA planning data entry transaction; irrelevant to condition type pricing and billing flows.
- **FBZP** — Bank determination configuration transaction; used for payment program settings, not condition types.
- **FBL1N** — Vendor line item display report; used for reporting open items rather than condition type configuration.
- **OBYZ** — Frequently confused with SD pricing config; while OBYZ is used for tax determination, SD pricing procedures are configured via V/08.

### 🧾 ACCOUNTING ENTRIES (with numbers)
**A. Goods Receipt (MIGO – Movement Type 101)**
*Scenario: Receive 100 pcs @ 10 EUR (Material 3000, V1 19% tax code)*
*Note: No tax is posted at Goods Receipt for stock materials.*
- Debit: Inventory (`BSX` 5190000000) = $1,000.00$ EUR ($100 \text{ pcs} \times 10.00 \text{ EUR}$)
- Credit: GR/IR Clearing (`WRX` 3215000000) = $1,000.00$ EUR ($100 \text{ pcs} \times 10.00 \text{ EUR}$)

**B. Invoice Receipt (MIRO)**
*Scenario: Invoice received for 1,000.00 EUR + 19% VAT ($190.00$ EUR)*
- Debit: GR/IR Clearing (`WRX` 3215000000) = $1,000.00$ EUR
- Debit: Input Tax (`MWS` 1540000000) = $190.00$ EUR ($1,000.00 \text{ EUR} \times 19\%$)
- Credit: Vendor AP = $1,190.00$ EUR ($1,000.00 \text{ EUR} + 190.00 \text{ EUR}$)

**C. Price Variance (PO at 1,000.00 EUR / Invoice at 1,050.00 EUR + 19% VAT)**
*Scenario: Invoice higher by 50.00 EUR + 19% VAT ($9.50$ EUR)*
- Debit: Price Difference (`PRD`) = $50.00$ EUR ($1,050.00 \text{ EUR} - 1,000.00 \text{ EUR}$)
- Debit: Input Tax (`MWS` 1540000000) = $9.50$ EUR ($50.00 \text{ EUR} \times 19\%$)
- Credit: Vendor AP = $1,109.50$ EUR ($1,050.00 \text{ EUR} + 59.50 \text{ EUR}$)

### 🧪 HOW TO TEST IT
1. Create a purchase order in `ME21N` (or sales order in `VA01`), verifying that condition types (`PB00`, `PR00`, `FRA1`) correctly populate from info records (`ME11`) or pricing condition records (`VK11`) under pricing procedure `ZGBE01`.
2. Post goods receipt via `MIGO` (movement type 101) and inspect the material document to ensure inventory (`BSX`) and GR/IR (`WRX`) accounts balance at $1,000.00$ EUR.
3. Process invoice verification via `MIRO`, verifying that input tax (`MWS`) calculates $190.00$ EUR on the $1,000.00$ EUR base and vendor AP credits $1,190.00$ EUR.
4. Review the Universal Journal line items in `FB03` / `ACDOCA` to confirm account determinations (`OBYC`, `VKOA`) and tax postings (`OBYZ`) are fully integrated.

### 🪤 TRAPS & THE ANSWER THAT WINS
- Trap: Assuming condition types post directly to FI during creation → Winning line: Condition types only calculate values in documents; they post to FI exclusively at billing or invoice verification via account determination keys like ERL or OBYC.
- Trap: Modifying standard delivered condition types directly → Winning line: Always copy standard condition types into the customer namespace starting with Z to maintain upgrade stability.

### 🎯 IF MY MIND GOES BLANK
Condition types control how pricing elements are calculated in sales orders or purchase orders. They are sequenced inside pricing procedures using transaction V/08. The main object name to remember is V/06 for defining them.

## 76. what is Copa

### 💡 SAY THIS FIRST
COPA lets us see exactly which product, customer and region generate profit in real time.

### 🗣️ DIRECT ANSWER TO SPEAK NOW
- **Core Concept:** It captures revenue, cost and margin per defined characteristics at the moment a billing document posts.
- **Key System Benefit:** S/4HANA stores the profitability line items in the universal journal ACDOCA, eliminating the reconciliation between the old CO‑PA tables CE1‑CE4 and FI.
- **Execution Strategy:** Build the operating concern (KEA0), assign the controlling area (KEKK), set the view mode (KEBD), map SD conditions (KE4I) and quantities (KE4M), then activate (KEKE).

### 📊 ARCHITECTURAL FLOW
```
1. OPERATING CONCERN KEA0
 define characteristics & value fields
 ↓
2. ASSIGN CONTROLLING KEKK
 link controlling area to concern
 ↓
3. SET VIEW MODE KEBD
 choose account‑based & costing‑based
 ↓
4. MAP SD CONDITIONS KE4I
 link pricing to value fields
 ↓
5. MAP QUANTITY FIELDS KE4M
 assign quantity to ABSMG
 ↓
6. ACTIVATE COPA KEKE
 status 4 = both views active
```

### ⚙️ CONFIG STEPS
1. **KEA0** — define operating concern, characteristics & value fields · Example: concern 1102, chars REGIO, LAND1, product; value fields ERLOS revenue, VV001 COGS · Where: SPRO ▸ Controlling ▸ Profitability Analysis ▸ Define Operating Concern
2. **KEKK** — assign controlling area to operating concern · Example: CA GB01 → concern 1102 · Where: SPRO ▸ Controlling ▸ Profitability Analysis ▸ Assign Controlling Area
3. **KEBD** — set view mode (account‑based & costing‑based) · Example: status 4 active for both views · Where: SPRO ▸ Controlling ▸ Profitability Analysis ▸ Define View
4. **KE4I** — map SD condition types to CO‑PA value fields · Example: Z001 → ERLOS, Z312 → discount field VV002, VPRS → COGS field VV001 · Where: SPRO ▸ Controlling ▸ Profitability Analysis ▸ Value Field Assignment
5. **KE4M** — assign quantity fields to CO‑PA (ABSMG) · Example: sales‑order quantity 1 stored in ABSMG · Where: SPRO ▸ Controlling ▸ Profitability Analysis ▸ Quantity Assignment
6. **KEKE** — activate CO‑PA, status 4 = both types active · Example: set status 4, save → billing writes to CE1‑CE4 · Where: SPRO ▸ Controlling ▸ Profitability Analysis ▸ Activate

### 🔧 DROP THESE OBJECT NAMES
- **KEA0** — operating concern definition
- **KEKK** — CA‑to‑concern assignment
- **KEBD** — view‑mode selection
- **KE4I** — condition‑to‑value mapping
- **KE4M** — quantity field linking
- **KEKE** — activation status 4
- **CE1‑CE4** — CO‑PA line‑item tables (S/4HANA)
- **ACDOCA** — universal journal source for account‑based view

### 🧾 ACCOUNTING ENTRIES
- Goods issue (VL02N): Dr 5111000000 COGS 150.00 / Cr 3102000000 Inventory 150.00 — PGI writes COGS into CO‑PA value field.
- Billing (VF01): Dr 120000 Customer 352.44, Dr 4411000000 Discount 50.23 / Cr 4111000000 Sales 346.40, Cr 157000 Tax 56.27 — creates CO‑PA revenue and discount fields.
- Costing‑based CO‑PA line (CE1): Qty 1, List Price 346.40, Discounts ‑50.23, Net Sales 296.17, COGS 150.00, Margin 146.17 — stored in CE1/CE2.

### 🧪 HOW TO TEST IT
1. Open **KEA0**, verify characteristics and value fields are present.
2. Create a sales order (VA01), post goods issue (VL02N) and billing (VF01) using list price 346.40 and 10 % discount.
3. Run **KE24** (account‑based) → confirm revenue, COGS and margin match the GL entries in **FBL3N/ACDOCA**.
4. Run **KE24** (costing‑based) → verify value fields list price, discount, net sales, COGS and margin equal the numbers posted in step 2.
5. Deactivate **KEKE**, post another billing, reactivate, and show the new posting appears only after activation.

### 🪤 TRAPS & THE ANSWER THAT WINS
- Trap: Assuming CO‑PA creates separate GL postings → Winning line: “CO‑PA only writes to CE tables; the GL impact stays in ACDOCA.”
- Trap: Believing account‑based and costing‑based are independent systems → Winning line: “Both read the same universal journal, so reconciliation is automatic.”

### 🎯 IF MY MIND GOES BLANK
COPA is profitability analysis per dimension.
It replaced the manual CE‑table‑to‑FI reconciliation.
Key object: **KEA0**.

## 77. how can you describe your experience based on the business requirement and solution

### 💡 SAY THIS FIRST
> My entire architecture approach is built on translating messy operational business requirements into clean, standard-first S/4HANA configurations,…

### 🗣️ DIRECT ANSWER TO SPEAK NOW

### 🗣️ THE 30-SECOND VERSION
When we launched our retail and e-commerce expansion at CYBEX, the business requirement was simple to state but complex to execute: spin up new store company codes across France, Germany, the US, and the UK that integrate clean with POS and OMS systems, while satisfying local tax and parallel accounting rules. My solution was to design a standardized rollout template in SAP S/4HANA using company code copies, configuring `FINSC_LEDGER` for 0L on IFRS and L1 on German HGB, and implementing automated subledger workflows for `F110` payment factories, `CAMT.053` bank statements, and country-specific tax engines like Avalara for the US (*Sumit_Kashyap_SAP_FICO_Solution_Architect_CV.pdf*). I owned the design from the business blueprints and functional specs through SIT, UAT, cutover, and hypercare, ensuring every posting tied back cleanly into our Lucanet consolidation package (*Sumit_Kashyap_SAP_FICO_Solution_Architect_CV.pdf*).

### 💼 PROOF I CAN CITE IF THEY PUSH
- **Retail & POS Integration Requirement:** When Cegid POS orders replicated every 15 minutes into SAP sales orders, my solution automated the delivery, goods issue, and billing while reconciling Adyen PSP tenders and prepayments via monthly files (*Sumit_Kashyap_SAP_FICO_Solution_Architect_CV.pdf*).
- **Parallel Accounting Statutory Requirement:** To meet German HGB local books and IFRS group reporting simultaneously, I configured `FINSC_LEDGER` with ledger-specific adjustments (`FB50L`), parallel depreciation areas, and financial statement versions for both HGB Bilanz/GuV and IFRS (*Sumit_Kashyap_SAP_FICO_Solution_Architect_CV.pdf*).

### 🪤 TRAPS
- **Trap:** Treating a business requirement as purely technical configuration without checking tax or audit impacts. -> **Winning line:** Every blueprint decision I make is anchored in statutory compliance, like ensuring GoBD and DART export readiness for German tax audits right from day one (*Sumit_Kashyap_SAP_FICO_Solution_Architect_CV.pdf*).
- **Trap:** Over-customising SAP when standard S/4HANA functionality already covers the edge case. -> **Winning line:** I push back on unnecessary Z-development by leveraging standard S/4HANA features like document splitting, extension ledgers, and standard IDoc interfaces first (*Sumit_Kashyap_SAP_FICO_Solution_Architect_CV.pdf*).

### 🎯 IF MY MIND GOES BLANK
I translate business blueprints into standard S/4HANA finance architectures. At CYBEX, I delivered five international rollouts by mapping operational needs—like POS replication, tax engines, and parallel ledgers—directly into clean SPRO configurations and automated banking workflows (*Sumit_Kashyap_SAP_FICO_Solution_Architect_CV.pdf*).

## 78. what is product costing

### 💡 SAY THIS FIRST
A standard cost estimate calculates what a product should cost by combining the quantity structure with activity rates and material prices.

### 🗣️ DIRECT ANSWER TO SPEAK NOW (speak aloud in ~30-45 secs)
- **Core Concept:** Product costing is used to find the internal cost of products and drive management accounting and inventory valuation for production.
- **Key System Benefit:** In S/4HANA, product cost planning and cost object controlling operate directly on the Universal Journal, integrating clean with Material Ledger for actual costing without legacy reconciliation gaps.
- **Execution Strategy:** The architecture requires cost center planning via KP06 and KP26, standard cost estimation through CK11N and CK40N, and settlement via CO88, backed by organisational definitions in OKKP.

### 📊 ARCHITECTURAL FLOW
```
1. STRUCTURE OKKP · OX18
 controlling area and plant assignment

 ↓
2. PLAN KP06 · KP26
 cost center dollars and activity rates loaded

 ↓
3. ESTIMATE CK11N · CK40N
 quantity structure plus prices rolled up

 ↓
4. RELEASE CK24
 mark and release standard cost to material master

 ↓
5. CLOSE KKAX · CO88
 calculate WIP and variances, settle to profitability

```

### ⚙️ CONFIG STEPS
1. **OKKP** — maintain the controlling area, currency, fiscal-year variant, and company-code assignment · Example: GB01 controlling area with currency EUR and version 0 · Where: SPRO ▸ Controlling ▸ General Controlling ▸ Maintain Controlling Area
2. **KS01** — create cost centers for production and support activities · Example: PRD01 production cost center assigned to hierarchy area · Where: SAP GUI ▸ Accounting ▸ Controlling ▸ Cost Center Accounting ▸ Master Data
3. **KA01** — create primary and secondary cost elements as G/L accounts · Example: Secondary cost element for internal activity allocation · Where: SAP GUI ▸ Controlling ▸ Cost Center Accounting ▸ Master Data
4. **KP06** — plan total dollars and costs by cost center and cost element · Example: Plan 50,000 in production cost center for overhead · Where: SAP GUI ▸ Controlling ▸ Cost Center Accounting ▸ Planning
5. **KP26** — define cost center activity quantities and rates · Example: Enter practical capacity and activity rates for mixing and baking · Where: SAP GUI ▸ Controlling ▸ Cost Center Accounting ▸ Planning
6. **OKTZ** — define cost component structure to break down material, labor, and overhead · Example: Cost component structure splitting raw materials and internal activities · Where: SPRO ▸ Controlling ▸ Product Cost Controlling ▸ Product Cost Planning ▸ Basic Settings for Material Costing
7. **CK11N** — create the material cost estimate using BOM and routing · Example: Cost estimate for finished good cookie package based on quantity structure · Where: SAP GUI ▸ Accounting ▸ Controlling ▸ Product Cost Controlling ▸ Product Cost Planning ▸ Material Costing
8. **CK24** — mark and release the standard cost estimate to update inventory valuation · Example: Release price for the current period into the material master · Where: SAP GUI ▸ Accounting ▸ Controlling ▸ Product Cost Controlling ▸ Product Cost Planning ▸ Environment ▸ Price Update

### ☕ DROP THESE OBJECT NAMES
- **OKKP** — controlling area configuration definition
- **KP06** — cost center cost planning transaction
- **KP26** — activity rate planning transaction
- **CK11N** — single material cost estimate creation
- **CK24** — price marking and releasing tool
- **KKAX** — WIP calculation at period close
- **CO88** — production order settlement transaction
- **ACDOCA** — universal journal line item table

### 🧾 ACCOUNTING ENTRIES
- Dr Production order 50000 / Cr Inventory raw materials 50000 — when raw materials are issued to the production order based on the bill of materials.
- Dr Production order 20000 / Cr Activity allocation 20000 — when internal activity rates from cost centers are confirmed on the production order.
- Dr Finished goods inventory 70000 / Cr Production output 70000 — when the finished goods are received into stock at standard cost.
- Dr Production variance 3000 / Cr Production order 3000 — when variances are settled at period close based on actual versus standard consumption.

### 🧪 HOW TO TEST IT
1. Open KP06 and KP26 to verify planned cost-center values and activity rates exist for the plant.
2. Run CK11N for a finished good material, review the cost component split, and execute CK24 to release the price.
3. Post a goods movement for raw material consumption and confirm activity confirmations on a production order using MIGO and CO15.
4. Execute KKAX and CO88 in test mode, then verify settlement documents and actual versus standard postings in ACDOCA and table SE16H.

### 🪤 TRAPS & THE ANSWER THAT WINS
- Trap: Planning activity rates at full theoretical capacity without accounting for downtime. → Winning line: Plan activity quantities based on practical installed capacity to prevent underestimated rates and unabsorbed overhead variances.
- Trap: Manually entering activity rates instead of using system calculations. → Winning line: Using system calculation preserves unit variances and enables rigorous actual-versus-plan analysis.

### 🎯 IF MY MIND GOES BLANK
Product costing calculates standard costs using BOMs, routings, and activity rates from cost centers planned in KP06 and KP26, releasing prices via CK24 to value inventory and settle variances.

## 79. how profitability analysis and copies connected

### 💡 SAY THIS FIRST
Profitability analysis connects sales orders and billing documents to market segments so you can analyze contribution margins by customer, product, or sales region.

### DIRECT ANSWER TO SPEAK NOW
Profitability Analysis (CO-PA) evaluates market segments—classified by products, customers, orders, sales organizations, or business areas—with respect to your company's profit and contribution margin. The connection between profitability analysis and copies or derivations is driven by how characteristics (like customer, product, and sales organization) are populated from the SD billing document (created via transaction VF01) into CO-PA. Derivation rules ensure these market segments are properly assigned so that business units can make informed internal accounting and decision-making choices across both costing-based and account-based profitability analysis.

### 📊 ARCHITECTURAL FLOW
```
1. SALES ORDER VA01
 no FI posting; pricing runs, profitability segment derived on the item

 ↓
2. GOODS ISSUE VL02N
 Dr COGS 150.00 / Cr Inventory 150.00

 ↓
3. BILLING F2 VF01
 Dr Customer 352.44, Dr Discounts 50.23, Cr Sales 346.40, Cr Output tax 56.27

 ↓
4. KE24 ACCOUNT-BASED KE24
 reads the P&L lines of the postings (ACDOCA); the G/L account is the value

 ↓
5. KE24 COSTING-BASED KE24
 reads characteristics + value fields; list price, discounts, net sales, COGS, margin

```

### ⚙️ CONFIG STEPS
1. **KEA0** — define the operating concern: characteristics and value fields · Example: Operating concern 1102 on controlling area 2018 (CYBEX runs GB01 combined) · Where: SPRO ▸ Controlling ▸ Profitability Analysis ▸ Structures ▸ Define Operating Concern
2. **KEKK** — assign the controlling area to the operating concern · Example: Controlling area 2018 gets operating concern 1102 · Where: SPRO ▸ Controlling ▸ Profitability Analysis ▸ Structures ▸ Assign Controlling Area to Operating Concern
3. **KEBD** — set the operating concern and choose the costing-based working mode · Example: Enter 1102 and pick costing-based or margin analysis view · Where: SPRO ▸ Controlling ▸ Profitability Analysis ▸ Tools ▸ Set Operating Concern
4. **KE4I** — assign SD condition types to CO-PA value fields · Example: Z001 list price, Z312 promo discount, and VPRS cost mapped to value fields · Where: SPRO ▸ Controlling ▸ Profitability Analysis ▸ Flows of Actual Values ▸ Initial Posting of Sales Documents ▸ Assign Condition Types
5. **KE4M** — assign SD quantity fields to value fields · Example: SD billed quantity mapped to ABSMG quantity field · Where: SPRO ▸ Controlling ▸ Profitability Analysis ▸ Flows of Actual Values ▸ Initial Posting of Sales Documents ▸ Transfer Quantities
6. **KEKE** — activate Profitability Analysis for the operating concern · Example: Active status set to 4 for both costing-based and account-based · Where: SPRO ▸ Controlling ▸ Profitability Analysis ▸ Structures ▸ Activate Profitability Analysis
7. **KER1** — define key figure schemes for reporting structures · Example: Key figure scheme 01 for revenue minus COGS equals contribution margin · Where: SPRO ▸ Controlling ▸ Profitability Analysis ▸ Information System ▸ Create Key Figure Scheme
8. **KE31** — create the profitability report for KE30 execution · Example: Region-wise Profitability report using Country, Region, and Company Code · Where: Controlling ▸ Profitability Analysis ▸ Information System ▸ Execute Profit Report

### 🔧 DROP THESE OBJECT NAMES
- **KEA0** — operating concern characteristics and value fields
- **KEKK** — assign operating concern to controlling area
- **KEBD** — set operating concern working view
- **KEKE** — activate profitability analysis status 4
- **KE4I** — assign SD condition types to value fields
- **KE4M** — transfer billing quantities to CO-PA
- **KEDR** — derive profitability segment on sales documents
- **GB01** — CYBEX live combined operating concern

### ACCOUNTING ENTRIES (with numbers)
Using a consistent example of a billing document for product P-100 sold to customer C-500:
- **Revenue Posting**:
 - Debit: Customer Receivables (Customer C-500) = $1,000.00
 - Credit: Revenue Account = $1,000.00
- **COGS Posting (at Billing via Cost of Sales Accounting)**:
 - Debit: COGS Account = $600.00
 - Credit: Inventory Account = $600.00
- **CO-PA Value Calculation**:
 - Revenue: $1,000.00
 - COGS: $600.00
 - Gross Margin = Revenue ($1,000.00) - COGS ($600.00) = $400.00
 - Margin % = Gross Margin ($400.00) / Revenue ($1,000.00) × 100 = 40.0%

### 🧪 HOW TO TEST IT
1. **KEA0 / KEKE** — Open KEA0 and KEKE to verify that the operating concern is active for both costing-based and account-based analysis.
2. **VF03** — Open billing document VF03, click Accounting, and check that the profitability document exists alongside FI and CO documents.
3. **KE24** — Run KE24 in costing-based mode to verify value fields like net sales, discounts, and COGS populated correctly from the billing request.
4. **FAGLL03H** — Run account-based line items in FAGLL03H and compare them against account-based KE24 to prove full reconciliation with ACDOCA.

### 🪤 TRAPS & THE ANSWER THAT WINS
- Trap: Assuming account-based CO-PA requires manual value field mapping like costing-based CO-PA does. → Winning line: Account-based CO-PA uses the G/L account directly from ACDOCA and needs no condition mapping.
- Trap: Forgetting to activate the operating concern via KEKE before posting billing documents. → Winning line: Documents posted before KEKE activation will never appear in CO-PA, so activation is a strict cutover prerequisite.

### 🎯 IF MY MIND GOES BLANK
Profitability analysis connects sales billing to market segments using characteristics and value fields. S/4HANA reconciles account-based CO-PA directly via ACDOCA while costing-based uses value fields. Object name: KEA0.

## 80. R2r end to end

### 💡 SAY THIS FIRST
I’ll walk you through a complete Record‑to‑Report flow from master data to close.

### 🗣️ DIRECT ANSWER TO SPEAK NOW
“I test end-to-end integration as a strict business-document chain from source subledger to ACDOCA. For Procure-to-Pay, I execute ME21N for the PO, MIGO for goods receipt, MIRO for supplier invoice, and F110 for automated payment. For Order-to-Cash, I execute VA01 for sales order, VL02N for delivery and Post Goods Issue, VF01 for billing, and F-28 for incoming payment. For Plan-to-Product, I execute KP06/KP26 for cost center and activity planning, CO01 for production order release, MIGO for component staging, CO15 for order confirmation, MB31 for goods receipt of finished goods, and KO88 for order settlement. I prove every financial impact in FB03 and ACDOCA, verifying subledger reconciliation through FBL1N, FBL5N, and FBL3N.”

### 📊 ARCHITECTURAL FLOW
```
1. LEGAL ENTITY OX15
 create company code TR02, currency TRY, local currency TRY

 ↓
2. CONTROLLING AREA OKKP
 define GB01, currency EUR, fiscal year variant K4

 ↓
3. GL MASTER DATA OBD4
 assign chart of accounts, create G/L accounts 400000 (Revenue) 500000 (COGS)

 ↓
4. ACCOUNT DETERMINATION OBYC
 map transaction keys to G/L accounts via valuation class

 ↓
5. POSTING FB01
 post journal entry, automatically updates ACDOCA

```

### ⚙️ CONFIG STEPS
1. **OBYC** — Map valuation class and transaction keys **BSX** (Inventory), **WRX** (GR/IR Clearing), **GBB** (Offsetting Entry/Consumption), and **PRD** (Price Differences) to approved G/L accounts. Where: SPRO ▸ Materials Management ▸ Valuation and Account Assignment ▸ Account Determination ▸ Configure Automatic Postings. Reference: MM account-determination workbook; test via **ME21N/MIGO/MIRO**.
2. **OMR6** — Set invoice quantity and price tolerance limits and block behavior. Example: An out-of-tolerance MIRO invoice (€120 vs €100 PO) is blocked for AP review. Reference: Signed LIV tolerance matrix; exact thresholds maintained per project rules.
3. **VKOA** — Determine revenue G/L accounts from chart of accounts, sales organization, customer/material account assignment groups, and account keys (e.g., **ERL**). Where: SPRO ▸ Sales and Distribution ▸ Basic Functions ▸ Account Assignment/Costing ▸ Revenue Account Determination. Reference: SD revenue-account mapping; validate via **VF01/VF03**.
4. **OB40** — Map tax account keys to input/output-tax G/L accounts for the configured tax procedure. Example: Billing tax line credits the output-tax G/L. Reference: Country tax design / tax-account matrix; rates and accounts are jurisdiction-specific.
5. **KP06 / KP26** — Configure cost center and activity type planning parameters for Product Costing. Where: SPRO ▸ Controlling ▸ Cost Center Accounting ▸ Planning. Reference: CO-CCA planning layout and activity rates.
6. **OX10 / OX17 / OBY6** — Verify plant definition, plant-to-company-code assignment, and company-code global parameters. Reference: Project organization-structure specification.

### ⚙️ CONFIG STEPS

### 🔧 DROP THESE OBJECT NAMES
- **OBYC** — automatic account determination for all FI postings
- **VKOA** — revenue account determination for SD billing
- **OB52** — period‑open/close control for each company code
- **CKMLCP** — cost‑object closing and settlement batch run
- **FAGL_FCV** — foreign‑currency revaluation for monetary items
- **ACDOCA** — universal journal table that stores every line item

### 🧾 ACCOUNTING ENTRIES
**FI–MM · Procure-to-Pay (€100 net purchase + €19 input VAT):**
- MIGO 101: Dr Inventory (BSX) €100.00 / Cr GR/IR Clearing (WRX) €100.00
- MIRO: Dr GR/IR Clearing (WRX) €100.00 + Dr Input VAT €19.00 / Cr Vendor Reconciliation €119.00
- F110 Payment: Dr Vendor Reconciliation €119.00 / Cr Bank-Clearing €119.00
- *Open Balance Calculations:*
 - GR/IR open balance remaining to clear: €100.00 - €100.00 = €0.00
 - Outstanding liability remaining: €119.00 - €119.00 = €0.00

**FI–SD · Order-to-Cash (€100 sale + €19 output VAT; €70 manufacturing cost):**
- VL02N PGI 601: Dr Cost of Goods Sold €70.00 / Cr Inventory (BSX) €70.00
- VF01 Billing: Dr Customer Reconciliation €119.00 / Cr Revenue (ERL) €100.00 + Cr Output VAT €19.00
- F-28 Receipt: Dr Bank €119.00 / Cr Customer Reconciliation €119.00
- *Open Balance Calculations:*
 - Customer open balance remaining: €119.00 - €119.00 = €0.00
 - Remaining inventory value change: €0.00 (movement fully processed)

**FI–PP · Plan-to-Product (€70 component issue, €100 finished goods receipt, €30 variance settlement):**
- MIGO 261 (Component Issue): Dr Work in Process / Consumption €70.00 / Cr Inventory €70.00
- MB31 (FG Receipt 101): Dr Finished Goods Inventory €100.00 / Cr Change in WIP / Production Settlement €100.00
- KO88 (Order Settlement): Dr Production Variance / COGS €30.00 / Cr Work in Process €30.00
- *Open Balance Calculations:*
 - Order balance remaining after settlement: €70.00 (WIP) - €100.00 (Receipt) + €30.00 (Settlement) = €0.00

### 🧪 HOW TO TEST IT
1. **P2P Testing:** Execute **ME21N** to create a €100 PO → Post Goods Receipt via **MIGO** (Movement 101) → Post Supplier Invoice via **MIRO** → Execute payment via **F110**. Inspect document flows in **ME23N**, **MIR4**, **FB03**, review **FBL3N** for **WRX** balance, and check **FBL1N** for vendor open items. Test price variance and block release via **MRBR**.
2. **O2C Testing:** Create sales order via **VA01** → Post Delivery and PGI via **VL02N** (€70 COGS) → Generate billing document via **VF01** (€100 revenue, €19 VAT) → Post incoming payment via **F-28** (€119). Inspect document flow in **VA03**, billing in **VF03**, FI document in **FB03**, customer items in **FBL5N**, and verify profitability segments in **ACDOCA**.
3. **PP Testing:** Plan cost and activity rates via **KP06/KP26** → Release production order via **CO01** → Issue components via **MIGO** (€70) → Confirm order via **CO15** → Post finished goods receipt via **MB31** (€100) → Settle production order via **KO88** (€30 variance). Validate all postings in **ACDOCA**.
4. For every chain, reconcile source quantities and values to financial totals, verify zero-balance clearing accounts, test one negative scenario (e.g., pricing error or insufficient stock), execute a document reversal, and trace errors through **SLG1**, **ST22**, and **SU53** before sign-off.

### 🔗 HOW IT INTEGRATES (FI / MM / SD / PP)
- **MM purchase order → Goods receipt (MIGO) → Dr Inventory / Cr GR/IR → Cost centre (CO) → ACDOCA, view in FAGLL03**
- **SD billing document → Dr Accounts Receivable / Cr Revenue → Profit centre (CO‑PA) → ACDOCA, view in KE5Z**
- **PP production order settlement → Dr WIP / Cr Production Variance → Internal order (CO) → ACDOCA, view in KO03**
- **Bank statement (FEBAN) → Dr Bank / Cr Vendor → Cash‑management ledger → ACDOCA, view in FF67**

### 📅 PERIOD‑END CLOSING SEQUENCE
1. **FB50** – post recurring accruals; ensures expenses are matched to revenue.
2. **OB52** – lock posting periods; prevents any further postings in the closed month.
3. **CKMLCP** – settle cost objects; moves variances to profitability analysis.
4. **FAGL_FCV** – revalue foreign‑currency items; reflects exchange‑rate impact in the ledger.
5. **FAGL_FCLOSE** – year‑end closing entries; transfers profit to retained earnings.

### ⚙️ CONFIG STEPS

### 💼 THE BUSINESS STORY I TELL
In my last greenfield rollout (NI01_FICO_Greenfield_Complete_v2‑1.pdf) the client needed a single R2R engine that could handle Turkish local GAAP and IFRS in parallel. I rejected the idea of separate ledgers per entity because it would double the reconciliation effort; instead I built one controlling area (GB01) with two parallel ledgers (0L = IFRS, 1L = HGB) and used OBYC to drive dual posting. We configured company code TR02, tested every posting through FB01, and ran month‑end close without any manual re‑entries. The business now produces statutory reports in under two hours and enjoys real‑time profit‑center insights.

### 🪤 TRAPS
- Assuming **VA01** or production order creation generates an immediate financial posting; actual G/L postings occur only at PGI, billing, goods movements, and settlement.
- Confusing **GR/IR (WRX)** with vendor reconciliation accounts, or revenue determination (**VKOA**) with tax determination (**OB40**).
- Forcing a clearing run or bypassing unlinked variances when reconciling partial quantities, currency translations, or tax conditions.
- Hardcoding organizational units, tax rates, G/L numbers, or settlement receivers instead of deriving them from signed-off configuration documents.

### 🎯 IF MY MIND GOES BLANK
“I trace the source document to its financial trigger, verify automatic account determination in OBYC, VKOA, or OB40, inspect the Universal Journal lines in FB03 and ACDOCA, and reconcile subledgers to G/L balances with a complete negative test and reversal verification.”

## 81. P2p full flow

### 💡 SAY THIS FIRST
Procure-to-pay is an automated chain where buying creates a commitment, receiving posts inventory, and invoicing clears the clearing account.

### 🗣️ DIRECT ANSWER TO SPEAK NOW
- **Core Concept:** Procure-to-pay manages the operational and financial lifecycle from purchase requisition to vendor payment, enforcing strict three-way matching between purchasing, inventory receipt, and invoice verification.
- **Key System Benefit:** S/4HANA integrates logistics and finance in real time inside the Universal Journal (ACDOCA), replacing legacy ECC reconciliation ledgers with instant visibility over commitments, stock valuations, and open liabilities.
- **Execution Strategy:** We drive this process through automatic account determination in OBYC using transaction keys BSX, WRX, and GBB, linked to material valuation classes and company code grouping codes in OMWD.

### 📊 ARCHITECTURAL FLOW
```
1. PURCHASE REQUISITION ME51N
 internal requirement for 100 pcs raw material

 ↓
2. PURCHASE ORDER ME21N
 commercial commitment to external vendor at EUR 10

 ↓
3. GOODS RECEIPT MIGO
 Dr Inventory 1,000 / Cr GR/IR 1,000 (BSX/WRX)

 ↓
4. INVOICE RECEIPT MIRO
 Dr GR/IR 1,000 / Cr Vendor 1,000 — three-way match

 ↓
5. PAYMENT PROGRAM F110
 Dr Vendor / Cr Bank — clearing open items

 ↓
6. PERIOD-END CHECK MB5S · FBL3N
 reconcile open GR/IR balances and inventory accounts

```

### ❓ WHAT I CLARIFY BEFORE I TOUCH CONFIG
- How many valuation groupings do we need? → Group plants by legal entity and logistics rules — Example: All German plants under one valuation grouping code in OMWD.
- Which transaction keys require special G/L assignment? → Every stock movement type must map to BSX, WRX, GBB, or PRD — Example: Raw material issues map to GBB-VBR.
- How do we handle price variances on invoice receipt? → Assign price difference key PRD so variances don't block inventory valuation — Example: EUR 0.20 unit variance hits PRD.
- What is the tolerance limit for automated invoice blocking? → Set percentage and absolute limits in OMR6 so minor variances auto-block for buyers — Example: EUR 50 absolute tolerance.

### ⚙️ CONFIG STEPS
1. **OX09** — define the plant, the physical manufacturing or storage location where materials are received · Example: Plant DE01 in Hamburg · Where: SPRO ▸ Enterprise Structure ▸ Definition ▸ Logistics - General ▸ Define, copy, delete, check plant
2. **OMWD** — define the valuation grouping code and assign it to your valuation area so plants share account determination rules · Example: Valuation grouping 0001 for plant DE01 · Where: SPRO ▸ Materials Management ▸ Valuation and Account Assignment ▸ Group Valuation Areas
3. **OMSK** — configure the material types, account category references, and valuation classes that link materials to G/L accounts · Example: Valuation class 3000 for raw materials · Where: SPRO ▸ Materials Management ▸ Valuation and Account Assignment ▸ Account Determination ▸ Account Determination Without Wizard
4. **OBYC** — maintain automatic account determination for inventory and logistics transaction keys (BSX, WRX, GBB, PRD) · Example: BSX linked to G/L 130000 for raw material inventory · Where: SPRO ▸ Financial Accounting ▸ General Ledger Accounting ▸ Periodic Processing ▸ Autom. Account Assignment ▸ Define and Configure Account Assignment
5. **OMR6** — set up invoice verification tolerance limits for price and quantity variances to control automatic blocking · Example: Tolerance key PP with 5% upper limit · Where: SPRO ▸ Materials Management ▸ Logistics Invoice Verification ▸ Invoice Block ▸ Set Tolerance Limits
6. **FBZP** — configure the payment program paying company codes, bank selection, and payment methods for outgoing vendor payments · Example: Payment method T for bank transfer in DE01 · Where: SPRO ▸ Financial Accounting ▸ Accounts Receivable and Accounts Payable ▸ Business Transactions ▸ Outgoing Payments ▸ Automatic Outgoing Payments ▸ Setup Payment Program for Country/Company Code

### ☕ DROP THESE OBJECT NAMES
- **OBYC** — MM-FI automatic account determination matrix
- **BSX** — inventory posting transaction key
- **WRX** — goods receipt invoice receipt clearing account
- **GBB** — offsetting entry for inventory posting
- **PRD** — price difference account key
- **OMWD** — valuation grouping code assignment
- **MIGO** — goods receipt and movement posting
- **MIRO** — logistics invoice verification

### 🧾 ACCOUNTING ENTRIES
- Goods Receipt (MIGO): Dr Inventory (BSX) 1,000 / Cr GR/IR Clearing (WRX) 1,000 — 100 pcs @ EUR 10.00 at goods receipt.
- Invoice Receipt (MIRO): Dr GR/IR Clearing (WRX) 1,000 / Cr Vendor 1,000 — three-way match complete against purchase order.
- Invoice with Variance (MIRO): Dr GR/IR Clearing (WRX) 1,000 + Dr Price Difference (PRD) 20 / Cr Vendor 1,020 — invoice received at EUR 10.20 per unit.
- Outgoing Payment (F110): Dr Vendor 1,020 / Cr House Bank Main Account 1,020 — settling open payable via automatic payment program.

### 🧪 HOW TO TEST IT
1. Create a purchase order in ME21N for 100 pieces of raw material at EUR 10.00 each.
2. Post the goods receipt in MIGO and inspect the generated FI document in FB03 confirming Dr BSX / Cr WRX.
3. Post the vendor invoice in MIRO matching the purchase order and verify GR/IR clearing account balance returns to zero.
4. Run the open item report FBL3N for the vendor and execute the GR/IR balance report in MB5S to verify period-end consistency.

### 🔗 HOW IT INTEGRATES (FI / MM / SD / PP)
- Purchase requisition (ME51N) → creates internal demand and commitments → captured in controlling cost objects → seen in ME5A.
- Goods receipt (MIGO) → Dr Inventory / Cr GR/IR → updates stock valuation and general ledger → seen in ACDOCA and FAGLL03.
- Vendor invoice (MIRO) → Dr GR/IR / Cr Vendor → updates accounts payable subledger and liability → seen in FB03 and FBL1N.
- Payment run (F110) → Dr Vendor / Cr Bank → clears open vendor items and updates bank ledger → seen in FBL1N and bank statements.

### 📅 PERIOD-END CLOSING SEQUENCE
1. **MB5S** — run GR/IR balance report to identify and investigate aged or unmatched goods receipts.
2. **MRBR** — release or review blocked invoices resulting from price or quantity variances.
3. **F.13** — run automatic clearing of cleared items for GR/IR and vendor clearing accounts.
4. **FAGLGVTR** — carry forward vendor and balance sheet account balances into the new fiscal year.

### 🩺 TROUBLESHOOTING — CONFIG, MASTER DATA OR TRANSACTION?
- Symptom: Goods receipt fails with account determination error message FF709 → it is configuration → check OBYC table for transaction key BSX and valuation class 3000 → fix G/L account assignment.
- Symptom: Material master missing valuation class during purchase order creation → it is master data → check MM03 accounting view for the material and plant → fix valuation class assignment.
- Symptom: Invoice blocked in MIRO due to price variance exceeding limits → it is transaction → check purchase order price vs vendor invoice price in ME23N → correct invoice price or release via MRBR.

### 💼 THE BUSINESS STORY I TELL
During our recent multi-company code rollout, the procurement team faced recurring month-end discrepancies between physical inventory and financial ledgers due to un-cleared GR/IR balances. I redesigned the procure-to-pay architecture by standardizing valuation grouping codes in OMWD and tightening OBYC account determination across all plants. We established strict three-way matching rules and automated monthly GR/IR clearing runs using MB5S and F.13. As a result, the finance team reduced open clearing balances by 85% and achieved automated, audit-ready period-end closes without manual journal entries.

### 🪤 TRAPS & THE ANSWER THAT WINS
- Trap: Assuming manual G/L entry is acceptable in logistics transactions to fix posting errors. → Winning line: Never bypass automatic account determination; we fix the OBYC matrix or the material master, never the accounting document.
- Trap: Treating the GR/IR clearing account as a general suspense bucket for unresolved vendor issues. → Winning line: GR/IR is a strict clearing account with a named operational owner and a mandatory month-end clearing routine.

### 🎯 IF MY MIND GOES BLANK
Procure-to-pay connects purchasing, inventory, and accounts payable through automated account determination. MIGO posts inventory and GR/IR, MIRO clears the clearing account via three-way match, and OBYC drives the underlying postings.
