## 82. Controlling config

### 💡 SAY THIS FIRST
When setting up controlling, I always align the controlling area to the company code first and establish our primary and secondary cost elements for tracking.

### 🗣️ DIRECT ANSWER TO SPEAK NOW (speak aloud in ~30-45 secs)
- **Core Concept:** Controlling configuration establishes internal managerial accounting structures to track costs, manage overhead, and analyze profitability across our organizational units.
- **Key System Benefit:** In S/4HANA, controlling entries post in real time alongside financial accounting into the Universal Journal table ACDOCA, completely eliminating the old COEP-to-BSEG reconciliation bottlenecks we faced in ECC.
- **Execution Strategy:** I drive this configuration primarily through transaction OKKP to define the controlling area and assign company codes, paired with KA06 for secondary cost elements and OKEON for cost center hierarchies.

### 📊 ARCHITECTURAL FLOW
```
ORG: OKKP controlling area OX18 company codes FY variant / CoA
↓
MASTER: FS00 cost elements (G/L) · KS01 cost centers · KSH1 hierarchy
KL01 activity types · KO01 internal orders · OKB9 defaults
↓
PLAN: KP06 costs · KP26 activity prices · KPF6 order planning
↓
ALLOCATE: KSU1/KSV1 cycles ► KSU5/KSV5 execution
↓
PRODUCT COSTING: OKTZ components · OKKN variant · CK11N/CK24
OMX1 material ledger · CKMLCP actual costing
↓
PROFITABILITY: KEA0 operating concern · KEDR derivation · KE51 profit centers
↓
PERIOD-END: KSII actual prices · CON2 revaluation · KO88/CO88 settlement · KE30/KE24 reports
↓
ACDOCA — one journal for FI and CO, no reconciliation ledger
```

### ⚙️ CONFIG STEPS
1. **OKKP** — create/maintain the controlling area: one chart of accounts, one fiscal-year variant, controlling-area currency; assign company codes in **OX18** — cross-company-code controlling only works with the same fiscal-year variant and chart. Where: SPRO ▸ Controlling ▸ General Controlling ▸ Organization. Reference: enterprise-structure sign-off.
2. **FS00** — cost elements are G/L accounts in S/4: primary cost/revenue elements carry a cost-element category on the G/L; secondary elements (categories 21 internal settlement, 31 order/project settlement, 41 overhead, 42 assessment, 43 internal activity allocation) are created as G/Ls — the ECC habit of separate masters is gone. Reference: chart-of-accounts design.
3. **KS01 + KSH1** — cost centers and the standard hierarchy (every cost center must sit in the hierarchy or it is invisible to allocations and reports); **OKB9** default account assignment per cost element / valuation area so postings never fail for a missing object. Reference: cost-center design list.
4. **KL01 + KP26** — activity types with unit, category and allocation cost element; plan activity prices in **KP26** (with **KP06** cost planning on the sender cost centers) — no price, no confirmation can value. Reference: activity-rate calculation from the planning round.
5. **KOT2 + OKO7** — internal-order types with settlement profile and allocation structure: receiver categories (cost center, asset, CO-PA segment), settlement cost elements, and the order status model that decides when an order may settle (**KO01/KO88** execute it). Reference: order-type design matrix.
6. **KSU1 / KSV1** — assessment and distribution cycles with segments: sender rules, receiver tracing factors (statistical key figures, percentages, actual costs), iteration switched on deliberately. Executed with **KSU5/KSV5**; cycle design is where month-end loops are prevented — ordered, non-overlapping segments, receivers validated before the run.
7. **OKTZ + OKKN** — product costing: cost component structure (OKTZ) splits material/labour/overhead; costing variant (OKKN) ties costing type, valuation variant and quantity structure (BOM/routing via strategy); **CK11N** calculates, **CK24** marks and releases the standard price. Reference: costing-sheet and overhead design.
8. **OMX1 + CKMLCP** — activate the Material Ledger per valuation area (mandatory in S/4) and configure actual costing: **CKMLCP** collects price and exchange-rate differences and posts them to consumption and ending inventory at period close. Reference: actual-costing position paper.
9. **KEA0 + KEDR** — CO-PA operating concern: characteristics and (for costing-based) value fields; account-based margin analysis runs on G/L accounts in ACDOCA and is the S/4 default; derivation rules in **KEDR**, PA transfer structures **KEI1** (billing) and **KEI2** (direct FI/MM postings) decide what reaches the segment. Reference: profitability design.
10. **KE51 + KCH1** — profit centers and the standard hierarchy; with document splitting, the profit center carries the segment for the segment balance sheet; **OKB9**/default assignments keep the profit center populated on every posting. Reference: segment-reporting requirement.
11. Period-end parameters: **KSII** actual activity price calculation, **CON2** order revaluation at actual prices, variance categories in the target-cost versions, settlement executed per order type (**KO88** individual / **CO88** collective) and **KKS2** variance analysis feeding them. Reference: close calendar.

### ⚙️ CONFIG STEPS

### ☕ DROP THESE OBJECT NAMES
- **OKKP** — controlling area definition and company code assignment
- **ACDOCA** — universal journal table combining FI and CO data
- **OKEON** — cost center standard hierarchy maintenance
- **KA06** — secondary cost element creation for allocations
- **CKMLCP** — material ledger actual costing run transaction
- **OBYC** — automatic account determination for material movements

### ACCOUNTING ENTRIES (WITH NUMBERS)
- **Activity confirmation (CO11N):**
 Formula: $40\text{ hours} \times €60/\text{hour} = €2,400$
 Dr Production order €2,400 / Cr Assembly cost center €2,400 — 40 h at the KP26 price of €60; valued by the activity type, posted to ACDOCA with order and cost center on one line.
- **Assessment (KSU5):**
 Formula: Total pool €8,500 allocated across receivers based on tracing factors
 Dr Receiver cost centers €8,500 / Cr Sender (IT services) €8,500 via the category-42 secondary element — sender nets to €0.00, each receiver line carries its tracing-factor share.
- **Order settlement (KO88):**
 Formula: Actual cost (€11,500) - Standard receipt cost (€10,000) = Variance €1,500
 Dr Price difference / variance €1,500 / Cr Production order €1,500 — order balance after settlement is $€11,500 - €11,500 = €0.00$, variance visible per category in KKS2.
- **Actual costing (CKMLCP):**
 Formula: Total collected PPD €3,200 allocated to Consumption (€2,100) and Ending Inventory (€1,100) [Check: $€2,100 + €1,100 = €3,200$]
 Dr/Cr Material Ledger adjustments of €2,100 to consumption and €1,100 to ending inventory — periodic unit price replaces the moving average at close, per material in CKM3.

### HOW TO TEST IT
1. **Assignment proof:** post **FB50** to a cost element with no CO object — it must fail (account assignment required); with **OKB9** default it lands on the designed cost center. Read it in **KSB1** and in **ACDOCA**.
2. **Planning-to-actual:** KP06/KP26 plan, confirm an activity (CO11N), compare plan vs actual price per activity in **KSBT**; run **KSII** and show the actual price replacing the planned one.
3. **Allocation:** run **KSU5** in test mode first — sender zero, receivers per tracing factor, no iterative loop errors; then update run and reconcile secondary-element totals to zero across the cycle.
4. **Costing chain:** CK11N a finished material, check the component split in **CK13N**, release with CK24, produce, settle with KO88 and prove the order ends at zero with the variance explained.
5. **Profitability tie-out:** bill the sale (VF01) and read the margin in **KE24/KE30** plus the account-based view in ACDOCA — revenue, COGS and margin tie to the FI documents to the cent; negative test: a characteristic with no KEDR rule lands on the dummy segment and is visible, never lost.

### 🔗 HOW IT INTEGRATES (FI / MM / SD / PP)
- MM invoice (MIRO) → Automatic account determination via OBYC → Cost center or material inventory object → ACDOCA, seen in FAGLL03H.
- SD billing document (VF01) → Revenue account determination via VKOA → CO-PA profitability segment → ACDOCA and KE24.
- Production order confirmation (CO15) → Actual activity allocation and material withdrawal → Production cost object controlling → ACDOCA and COGI.

### 📅 PERIOD-END CLOSING SEQUENCE
1. **KA02** — master-data check to ensure all new cost centers and cost elements are active.
2. **KB61** — direct activity allocation corrections and manual cost reposting.
3. **KSU5** — run assessment cycles to allocate overhead costs using statistical key figures.
4. **KKAO** — calculate work in process (WIP) for open production orders.
5. **KSII** — calculate actual activity prices based on incurred cost center expenses.
6. **KKS1** — execute variance analysis for completed production orders.
7. **KO8G** — settle internal orders and production orders to final receivers.
8. **CKMLCP** — run material ledger actual costing and single-level price determination.
9. **F.01** — generate financial statements and reporting for period close sign-off.

## 83. how do you set up OB YC config what percentage

### 💡 SAY THIS FIRST
Automatic account determination in MM via OBYC links material movements to general ledger accounts using transaction keys.

### 📖 THE STORY, STEP BY STEP
1. OBYC is the central configuration transaction where you assign general ledger accounts to inventory postings, goods receipts, and invoice verifications based on valuation modifiers and account grouping codes.
 - SAP Object and T-code: T-code OBYC, transaction table T030.
 - Running Example: For our Cybex retail rollout (company code TR02, currency TRY), we post an inventory receipt for shoes valued at TRY 10,000.
 - Next Question: But who decides which valuation class triggers which G/L account? That is driven by the material master valuation class and the transaction key.

2. You define the valuation classes in the material master (MM01/MM02) and link them through account modification constants like GBB for offsetting entries in inventory.
 - SAP Object and T-code: Material master view Accounting 1 (MM01), transaction OBYC under modifier GBB (General Posting).
 - Running Example: Material 400001 (Leather Shoes) has valuation class 7920 (Finished Goods), which maps via OBYC for modifier VAY to inventory account 130100.
 - Next Question: How does the system know which chart of accounts to use for these automatic entries?

3. The system reads the chart of accounts assigned to your company code in OB62, and then OBYC maps the chart of accounts to the transaction keys like BSX for inventory and WRX for GR/IR clearing.
 - SAP Object and T-code: T-code OB62 for chart of accounts assignment, OBYC for table T030 mapping.
 - Running Example: For chart of accounts INT, transaction key BSX links valuation class 7920 to G/L account 130100 (Inventory Raw/Finished) with an amount of TRY 10,000.
 - Next Question: What are the exact accounting entries produced when a goods receipt is posted against this configuration?

### 🖼️ THE WHOLE THING IN ONE PICTURE
```
GOODS RECEIPT: MIGO, 100 pairs of shoes
↓
Material 400001 = Valuation Class 7920
↓
OBYC Transaction Keys: BSX (Inventory) & WRX (GR/IR)
↓
Posting: Dr Inventory TRY 10,000 / Cr GR/IR TRY 10,000
```

### 🧮 THE NUMBERS
- Quantity: 100 units
- Unit Price: TRY 100.00
- Total Inventory Posting: 100 × 100 = TRY 10,000
- BSX Debit: TRY 10,000 (Inventory Account 130100)
- WRX Credit: TRY 10,000 (GR/IR Clearing Account 210500)
- Result: Perfectly balanced goods receipt posting driven entirely by OBYC automatic account determination without manual G/L selection.

### ⚠️ IF THE QUESTION CONTAINS A WRONG ASSUMPTION
Careful — OBYC does not store a percentage for automatic account determination; it stores general ledger account assignments mapped to transaction keys, valuation groupings, and account modification constants. The percentages or values come entirely from the transactional documents like purchase orders, material prices, and goods receipt quantities.

### 🧠 THE FIVE THINGS TO REMEMBER
- OBYC uses transaction keys like BSX for inventory and WRX for GR/IR clearing to automate posting entries.
- Valuation grouping codes (OMWM) group plant-level valuations together to simplify OBYC table maintenance across multiple sites.
- Valuation classes in the material master act as the bridge between material types and G/L account assignment.
- Chart of accounts assignment via OB62 dictates which OBYC rules are evaluated during MM transaction processing.
- Account modification constants (such as GBB for offsetting entries) allow granular splitting of inventory postings based on movement types.

### 🗣️ DIRECT ANSWER TO SPEAK NOW
“I configure MM-FI automatic account determination via OBYC to link valuation classes and material movements to General Ledger accounts, ensuring real-time integration between Inventory Management and Financial Accounting. In S/4HANA, this maps material subledger events directly to ACDOCA. For a standard material procurement costing 1,000 USD with a 5% standard variance or price difference, OBYC ensures the offsetting entries post correctly without manual intervention.”

### 📊 ARCHITECTURAL FLOW
```text
Material Movement (MIGO) / Invoice (MIRO)
 ↓
Valuation Grouping Code & Valuation Class
 ↓
OBYC Transaction Key (e.g., BSX, WRX, PRD)
 ↓
Chart of Accounts + Valuation Modifier
 ↓
G/L Account Determination (ACDOCA / Universal Journal)
```

### ⚙️ CONFIG STEPS
1. **Define Valuation Area** — (OMWD): Set valuation level at Company Code or Plant level and assign valuation grouping codes.
2. **Define Valuation Classes** — (OMSK): Group materials with similar accounting requirements (e.g., Raw Materials, Finished Goods).
3. **Configure Account Determination** — (OBYC): Maintain automatic posting accounts for transaction keys:
 - **BSX** (Inventory Posting): Debit/Credit Inventory G/L (e.g., 1,000 USD).
 - **WRX** (GR/IR Clearing): Credit GR/IR Clearing G/L upon goods receipt (1,000 USD).
 - **PRD** (Price Differences): Post purchase price variances or revaluation differences.
 - **GBB** (Offsetting Entry for Inventory Posting): Assign modifiers (e.g., VAY, BSA) for consumption or scrap postings.
4. **Assign Tax Procedures & Codes** — (OBBG, FTXP): Ensure integrated tax determination if applicable.
5. **Check Automatic Postings** — (OMWN): Verify transaction key completeness and simulation.

### 🔧 DROP THESE OBJECT NAMES
- **FD32** — Classic FI-AR credit management transaction (deprecated in S/4HANA; use UKM_* transactions).
- **KEU1** — CO-PA costing sheet / assessment cycle transaction (irrelevant for MM-FI OBYC inventory account determination).

### 🧾 ACCOUNTING ENTRIES
- **Goods Receipt (MIGO):**
 - Debit: Inventory Raw Materials G/L (BSX) = 1,000.00 USD
 - Credit: GR/IR Clearing G/L (WRX) = 1,000.00 USD
- **Invoice Receipt (MIRO) with 50.00 USD Variance:**
 - Debit: GR/IR Clearing G/L (WRX) = 1,000.00 USD
 - Debit: Price Difference G/L (PRD) = 50.00 USD
 - Credit: Vendor Account (AP Subledger / Reconciliation) = 1,050.00 USD
- **Net Inventory Asset Balance Impact:** 1,000.00 USD (Inventory) + 50.00 USD (Variance Expensed/Capitalized) - 1,050.00 USD (Liability) = 0.00 USD net imbalance.

### 👤 HOW TO TEST IT
1. Create a purchase order in ME21N for a valuated material for 1,000 USD.
2. Post a Goods Receipt in MIGO against the PO; verify via FB03 that G/L accounts for BSX and WRX are hit correctly.
3. Post the Vendor Invoice in MIRO with a 50.00 USD price variance; verify that transaction key PRD triggers the variance posting and updates ACDOCA.
4. Run F.13 or OBR4 / automatic clearing if required to clear the GR/IR clearing account (WRX balance = 1,000.00 USD - 1,000.00 USD = 0.00 USD).

### 🪤 TRAPS
- Omitting valuation grouping code assignment in OMWD, which breaks OBYC lookup tables.
- Failing to maintain valuation classes in OMSK for newly created material master records, resulting in MIGO error message M7091 ("Account determination for entry... not possible").
- Hardcoding company codes without leveraging chart of accounts level templates in OBYC.

### 🎯 IF MY MIND GOES BLANK
OBYC is the MM-FI integration transaction for automatic account determination. It maps transaction keys and valuation classes to G/L accounts. It replaced manual G/L coding for logistics movements using table T030.

## 84. Partner profile idoc setup

### 💡 SAY THIS FIRST
Partner profiles control inbound and outbound IDoc communication by linking partner types to message types, ports, and process codes.

### 🗣️ DIRECT ANSWER TO SPEAK NOW (speak aloud in ~30-45 secs)
- **Core Concept:** Partner profiles define the interchange rules for electronic data exchange between SAP and external trading partners or systems like Hellmann 3PL or Cegid POS.
- **Key System Benefit:** In S/4HANA, partner profiles orchestrate asynchronous B2B and A2A communication directly into the Universal Journal, replacing legacy ECC batch interfaces with real-time Idoc processing.
- **Execution Strategy:** The entire setup is driven through transaction WE20, linking partner numbers, partner types, inbound/outbound parameters, message types, and process codes such as IDOC_INPUT_INVOIC.

### 📊 ARCHITECTURAL FLOW
```
1. PORT DEFINITION WE21
 define tRFC or XML file ports for external systems

 ↓
2. LOGICAL SYSTEM BD54 · SCC4
 define logical destination for partner communication

 ↓
3. PARTNER PROFILE WE20
 configure inbound/outbound parameters, message types

 ↓
4. PROCESS CODE WE42 · WE41
 link inbound message type to function module

 ↓
5. TEST MONITORING WE02 · WE05
 verify IDoc status and posting execution

```

### CONFIG STEPS
1. **Define Logical Systems** — `BD54` (Define logical system names for SAP and external partner systems).
2. **Assign Logical System to Client** — `SCC4` (Map client to logical system for cross-system communication).
3. **Configure RFC Destinations** — `SM59` (Establish RFC connections for type T/G/H between SAP and middleware/external systems).
4. **Maintain Port Definitions** — `WE21` (Set up transactional RFC ports or file ports for IDoc transfer).
5. **Maintain Partner Profiles** — `WE20` (Define partner type KU/LI/LS, assign outbound parameters like message type `ORDERS`, basic type `ORDERS05`, output mode, and inbound parameters with process codes like `ORDE`).
6. **Assign Serialisation / Distribution Channels** — `BD64` (Maintain distribution model for ALE communication if required).

### CONFIG STEPS

### 🔧 DROP THESE OBJECT NAMES
- **WE20** — partner profile maintenance transaction
- **WE21** — port definition for idoc communication
- **WE02** — idoc display and status monitoring
- **WE42** — inbound process code definition
- **BD54** — logical system definition for partner routing
- **WEL1** — idoc accounting integration rules

### ACCOUNTING ENTRIES
- **Scenario:** Inbound Customer Order IDoc (`ORDERS05`) generating a Sales Order in SD, eventually leading to billing and an accounting posting.
- **Example Invoice Value:** $10,000.00 USD
- **Accounting Entry at Billing (Post-IDoc workflow):**
 - Debit: Customer Receivables (`KNA1` / Reconciliation Account) = $10,000.00 USD
 - Credit: Revenue Account = $10,000.00 USD
- **Formula:**
 $$\text{Open Balance} = \text{Invoice Amount} - \text{Clearing Amount} = \$10,000.00 - \$0.00 = \$10,000.00\text{ USD}$$

### HOW TO TEST IT
1. Trigger or simulate an outbound/inbound IDoc (e.g., via `WE19` - Test Tool for IDoc Processing).
2. Verify IDoc status and flow using `WE02` (Display IDocs) or `WE05` (IDoc List).
3. Check error handling and reprocess failed IDocs using `BD87` (Inbound Processing Status / Error Reprocessing).
4. Verify the resulting application document in `FB03` or SD/MM transaction depending on the message type, confirming update in `ACDOCA`.

### 🔗 HOW IT INTEGRATES (FI / MM / SD / PP)
- Inbound invoice IDoc (INVOIC) → creates MM-FI vendor invoice via MIRO logic → posts to vendor open items → seen in FBL1N and ACDOCA.
- Outbound delivery IDoc (SHPCON) → updates SD delivery status → triggers billing due list → seen in VF04.
- POS sales IDoc → posts retail revenue and payment tenders → updates Universal Journal profitability → seen in FAGLL03H.

### 📅 PERIOD-END CLOSING SEQUENCE
1. **WE02** — review stuck IDocs in status 51 or 64 before running financial close.
2. **BD87** — reprocess failed IDocs to ensure all operational transactions are posted.
3. **F.13** — execute automatic clearing for cleared vendor and customer open items.

### CONFIG STEPS

### 💼 THE BUSINESS STORY I TELL
During our Cybex rollouts integrating Hellmann 3PL and Cegid POS, partner profiles were the backbone of our asynchronous data pipelines. The client initially wanted custom file-to-table interfaces, but I enforced standard IDoc partner profiles via WE20 using tRFC ports through SAP CPI. I configured inbound process codes to map POS sales and 3PL invoices directly into the financial books without manual intervention. We tested edge cases using WE19 test tool injections, ensuring every error status 51 routed correctly to monitoring queues. This architecture gave the business a resilient, real-time integration layer that processed thousands of daily transactions clean into ACDOCA.

### 🪤 TRAPS & THE ANSWER THAT WINS
- Trap: Assuming partner profiles only need outbound configuration when building B2B interfaces. → Winning line: Inbound parameter setup with correct process codes in WE20 is critical for posting vendor invoices and POS sales automatically.
- Trap: Hardcoding test partner numbers in production profile setups. → Winning line: Partner profiles must strictly map to production logical systems defined in BD54 to prevent routing failures during cutover.

### 🎯 IF MY MIND GOES BLANK
Partner profiles link partner numbers to message types and ports in WE20. They replaced legacy batch interfaces with real-time IDoc processing. Use transaction WE20 and WE02 for monitoring.

## 85. how do you config complete mmfi cycle

### 💡 SAY THIS FIRST
Configuring the complete MM-FI cycle requires linking material valuation classes to automatic account determination keys through OBYC.

### 📖 THE STORY, STEP BY STEP
1. Define the valuation grouping code in transaction OMWD so plants share or isolate their account determination based on company code logic.
 - SAP object: OMWD (Valuation Grouping Code).
 - Running example: Plant 1000 uses valuation grouping code 0001 to drive raw material postings.
 - Design question: "Do plants share valuation?" → "Yes, across the German entity" — Example: Grouping code 0001 for all plants in company code 1000.

2. Set up valuation classes in the material master to categorise inventory types like raw materials versus trading goods.
 - SAP object: MM03 (Material Master) / SPRO Material Valuation.
 - Running example: Material MAT-01 uses valuation class 3000 for raw materials, linking it to the raw material inventory account.
 - Design question: "How many valuation classes?" → "We align them strictly by material type" — Example: Class 3000 for Raw Materials, 3100 for Finished Goods.

3. Configure automatic account determination in transaction OBYC using transaction keys like BSX for inventory, WRX for GR/IR clearing, and GBB for offsetting entries.
 - SAP object: OBYC (Automatic Account Determination).
 - Running example: BSX is mapped to G/L 130000 (Inventory Raw Materials), and WRX is mapped to G/L 210000 (GR/IR Clearing).
 - Design question: "Which G/L accounts receive inventory changes?" → "Standard stock accounts mapped via OBYC keys" — Example: BSX for stock, WRX for the purchasing clearing liability.

4. Post the purchase order and goods receipt via MIGO, which triggers the automatic FI posting without manual journal entries.
 - SAP object: MIGO (Goods Movement).
 - Running example: Receiving 100 pcs of MAT-01 at EUR 10 each posts Dr Inventory 1,000 / Cr GR/IR 1,000 using keys BSX and WRX.
 - Design question: "Who posts the inventory receipt?" → "MM module via movement type 101" — Example: MIGO execution creates financial document automatically.

5. Execute invoice receipt via MIRO to perform the three-way match and clear the GR/IR clearing account.
 - SAP object: MIRO (Logistics Invoice Verification).
 - Running example: Vendor invoice arrives for EUR 1,000, posting Dr GR/IR 1,000 / Cr Vendor 1,000.
 - Design question: "How do we handle invoice price variances?" → "Route them to price difference accounts via key PRD" — Example: EUR 20 variance hits PRD automatically.

### 🖼️ THE WHOLE THING IN ONE PICTURE
```
PO CREATION (ME21N)
↓
GOODS RECEIPT (MIGO)
Dr Inventory 1,000 / Cr GR/IR 1,000 (BSX/WRX)
↓
OBYC AUTOMATIC DETERMINATION
Valuation Class 3000 → G/L Accounts
↓
INVOICE RECEIPT (MIRO)
Dr GR/IR 1,000 / Cr Vendor 1,000
```

### 🧮 THE NUMBERS
- Quantity: 100 pcs
- Purchase Price: EUR 10.00 each
- Inventory Value (BSX): 100 * 10.00 = EUR 1,000.00 debit
- GR/IR Clearing (WRX): 100 * 10.00 = EUR 1,000.00 credit
- Invoice Verification (MIRO): Dr GR/IR EUR 1,000.00 / Cr Vendor EUR 1,000.00 — zero balance on clearing account.

### ⚠️ IF THE QUESTION CONTAINS A WRONG ASSUMPTION
Careful — users do not type G/L accounts manually during goods receipts or invoice verifications; OBYC and material valuation classes determine them automatically.

### 🧠 THE FIVE THINGS TO REMEMBER
- OBYC is the central configuration hub linking MM transaction keys to FI General Ledger accounts.
- Valuation grouping codes (OMWD) control whether plants share or separate account determination rules.
- Material master valuation classes categorize inventory types to ensure correct posting accounts.
- MIGO triggers the goods receipt posting (Dr Inventory / Cr GR/IR) automatically via movement type 101.
- MIRO executes the three-way match, clearing the GR/IR account and posting the liability to the vendor.

### 🗣️ DIRECT ANSWER TO SPEAK NOW
- **Core Concept:** FI-MM integration is automatic account determination: every goods movement and invoice in MM posts to FI without anyone typing a G/L account. OBYC holds the matrix — valuation class from the material master and valuation grouping code from OMWD decide which G/L accounts a movement hits: BSX for inventory, WRX for GR/IR clearing, GBB for goods-issue offsets (e.g., GBB-VBR for consumption to cost centers), PRD for price differences. MIGO creates the FI document at goods receipt, MIRO clears GR/IR at invoice receipt, and the three-way match (PO = GR = IR) is the control that makes it auditable.
- **Key System Benefit:** Because the posting logic is deterministic and flows directly into ACDOCA in S/4HANA, inventory values in FI and MM agree by design — period-end becomes GR/IR review (MB5S, MRBR), not reconciliation between two disparate modules.
- **Execution Strategy:** Design order: chart of accounts and valuation grouping code (OMWD), valuation classes on material masters (MM01/MM02/MM03), OBYC transaction keys per valuation class, then test the full chain PO (ME21N) → GR (MIGO) → IR (MIRO) → payment (F110) with one material of each valuation class before rollout sign-off.

### 📊 ARCHITECTURAL FLOW
```text
1. PURCHASE ORDER ME21N
 100 pcs @ EUR 10 — no FI posting yet
 ↓
2. GOODS RECEIPT MIGO (Mov. Type 101)
 Dr Inventory (BSX) 1,000 / Cr GR/IR (WRX) 1,000
 ↓
3. INVOICE RECEIPT MIRO
 Dr GR/IR 1,000 / Cr Vendor 1,000 — three-way match
 ↓
4. PAYMENT F110
 Dr Vendor / Cr Bank — AP subledger clears
 ↓
5. PROVE MB5S · FBL3N
 GR/IR balance and inventory account agree
```

### ⚙️ CONFIG STEPS
1. **OBYC** — maintain the account determination matrix per transaction key and valuation class — this is the heart of FI-MM · Example: BSX: inventory account for valuation class 3000 (raw materials); WRX: one GR/IR clearing account; GBB-VBR: consumption account for goods issue to cost centers · Ref: SPRO ▸ Materials Management ▸ Valuation and Account Assignment ▸ Account Determination.
2. **OMWD** — set the valuation grouping code per valuation area so plants that share one determination are grouped deliberately, not by accident · Example: All German plants group under one code and share the OBYC matrix; the Turkish plant groups separately with its own accounts · Ref: SPRO ▸ Materials Management ▸ Valuation and Account Assignment.
3. **MM03** — assign the correct valuation class and price control (S standard or V moving average) on every material master — wrong class, wrong account, every time · Example: A raw material on class 3000 posts to the raw-material inventory account; a trading good on class 3100 posts to its own · Ref: SAP GUI ▸ Logistics ▸ Materials Management ▸ Material Master.
4. **MIGO** — post goods receipt against the PO and read the FI document it creates automatically · Example: 100 pcs @ EUR 10: Dr Inventory (BSX) 1,000 / Cr GR/IR (WRX) 1,000 — quantity and value enter together · Ref: Logistics ▸ Materials Management ▸ Inventory Management ▸ Goods Movement.
5. **MIRO** — post the vendor invoice against the same PO and let the three-way match clear GR/IR · Example: Invoice at EUR 10.20: Dr GR/IR 1,000 + Dr Price difference (PRD) 20 / Cr Vendor 1,020 — the difference is visible, never buried · Ref: Logistics ▸ Materials Management ▸ Logistics Invoice Verification.
6. **MRBR** — release blocked invoices only after the block reason (price, quantity, date) is resolved at source · Example: A quantity-blocked invoice stays out of F110 until the GR is corrected — the block is the control working, not an error · Ref: Logistics Invoice Verification ▸ Release Blocked Invoices.
7. **MB5S** — run the GR/IR account balance list at period end and clear or explain every aged line · Example: The month-end GR/IR list shows only genuine open receipts; anything old gets a named owner · Ref: Logistics ▸ Materials Management ▸ Purchasing ▸ Purchase Order ▸ List Displays.

### 🔧 DROP THESE OBJECT NAMES
- **OBYC** — MM→FI account determination matrix.
- **BSX** — transaction key: inventory posting.
- **WRX** — transaction key: GR/IR clearing.
- **GBB** — transaction key: offsetting for goods movements (e.g., GBB-VBR for consumption).
- **PRD** — transaction key: price differences.
- **OMWD** — valuation grouping code.
- **MIGO** — goods receipt / movement.
- **MIRO** — invoice verification.
- **MRBR** — release blocked invoices.
- **MB5S** — GR/IR balance list.

### 🧾 ACCOUNTING ENTRIES
- Goods receipt (MIGO, Movement Type 101): Dr Inventory (BSX) EUR 1,000 / Cr GR/IR (WRX) EUR 1,000 — calculation: $100\text{ pcs} \times \text{EUR } 10 = \text{EUR } 1,000$, no vendor line yet.
- Invoice (MIRO) at agreed price: Dr GR/IR (WRX) EUR 1,000 / Cr Vendor EUR 1,000 — calculation: $100\text{ pcs} \times \text{EUR } 10 = \text{EUR } 1,000$, three-way match complete, GR/IR remaining balance = $\text{EUR } 1,000 - \text{EUR } 1,000 = \text{EUR } 0$.
- Invoice with price increase to EUR 10.20: Dr GR/IR (WRX) EUR 1,000 + Dr Price difference (PRD) EUR 20 / Cr Vendor EUR 1,020 — calculation: Invoice amount = $100\text{ pcs} \times \text{EUR } 10.20 = \text{EUR } 1,020$; clearing GR/IR = $\text{EUR } 1,000$; variance = $\text{EUR } 1,020 - \text{EUR } 1,000 = \text{EUR } 20$ hitting PRD under standard price.
- Goods issue to cost center (MIGO, Movement Type 201): Dr Consumption (GBB-VBR) EUR 1,000 / Cr Inventory (BSX) EUR 1,000 — calculation: $100\text{ pcs} \times \text{EUR } 10 = \text{EUR } 1,000$, cost center sees the posting via CO.

### 🧪 HOW TO TEST IT
1. Create PO (ME21N) for 100 pcs @ EUR 10, receive in MIGO (Mov. Type 101), and prove the FI document (Dr BSX EUR 1,000 / Cr WRX EUR 1,000) in FB03 before any invoice exists.
2. Post MIRO at EUR 10 and at EUR 10.20 and show both the clean match and the PRD difference document.
3. Run MB5S and agree the GR/IR balance to FBL3N on the WRX account; clear one aged item end to end.
4. Block one invoice deliberately (quantity), release it in MRBR after correcting the GR, and prove F110 then pays it.

### 🪤 TRAPS
- Trap: Maintaining G/L accounts directly in MIGO/MIRO documents. → Winning line: Nobody types accounts in MM — OBYC plus the valuation class decides; I fix the matrix, not the document.
- Trap: Treating one GR/IR account as a generic dump with no period-end review. → Winning line: WRX is a clearing account with an owner and a month-end list (MB5S), not a suspense account.
- Trap: Blaming FI for a wrong inventory value. → Winning line: Value follows price control and valuation class in the material master — I start the analysis in MM03 and OBYC.

### 🔗 CROSS-RELATED — FIXED, READY TO ASK NEXT
- HGB vs IFRS — how do parallel ledgers answer both from one document?
- How will you set up a company code for a new-country rollout?
- How does the Universal Journal (ACDOCA) change the month-end close?

### 🎯 IF MY MIND GOES BLANK
MM-FI integration relies on OBYC automatic account determination driven by valuation classes and movement types.
It replaced manual inventory journal entries with automated postings from MIGO and MIRO.
Key objects include OBYC, OMWD, BSX, and WRX.

## 86. can you tell me how Turkey configure setup

### 💡 SAY THIS FIRST
When rolling out our Turkish entity, I first locked down the legal, tax, and withholding setup before copying the company code and linking the plants.

### 🗣️ DIRECT ANSWER TO SPEAK NOW (speak aloud in ~30-45 secs)
- **Core Concept:** Setting up a country rollout like Turkey requires configuring legal entity definitions, local chart of accounts links, statutory tax codes, and intercompany clearing so transactions comply with local regulations while feeding the group ledger.
- **Key System Benefit:** In S/4HANA, the Universal Journal (ACDOCA) handles parallel ledgers automatically, allowing local Turkish GAAP reporting alongside IFRS without maintaining a disconnected parallel system.
- **Execution Strategy:** I drive the setup using enterprise structure transactions like OX15 and EC01, global parameters in OBY6, tax maintenance in FTXP, and automatic cross-company clearing in OBYA.

### 📊 ARCHITECTURAL FLOW
```
1. LEGAL DESIGN OX15 · EC01
 company, legal entity, country, currency and language

 ↓
2. STRUCTURE OX16 · OX18 · OKKP
 company code to company, plant and controlling area

 ↓
3. FI GLOBAL SETTINGS OBY6 · OBBP · FBN1
 currency, fiscal year, periods, tolerances and number ranges

 ↓
4. LOCALIZATION FTXP · OB40 · FBZP
 tax procedure/codes, payment methods, house bank and formats

 ↓
5. INTEGRATION OBYC · VKOA · OKB9
 inventory, revenue, COGS and account assignment determination

 ↓
6. INTERCOMPANY OBYA · VF01 (IV) · FBICR3
 cross-company supply, IC billing and reconciliation proven

 ↓
7. CUTOVER + CLOSE LTMC · OB52 · F.01
 open items, balances, assets, first close and sign-off

```

### ❓ WHAT I CLARIFY BEFORE I TOUCH CONFIG
- How many legal entities and company codes are we standing up? → One legal company code per distinct tax jurisdiction — Example: TR02 for our Turkish trading entity.
- Which local currency and parallel currency are required? → Local currency TRY for statutory reporting, with group currency EUR maintained in ledger 0L — Example: TRY for local books and EUR for group consolidation.
- Are we using a separate local chart of accounts or extending the group chart? → We extend the group chart of accounts and use alternative account numbers for local statutory reporting — Example: Group CoA with local alternative account keys mapped.
- What is the specific tax and withholding requirement for the country? → Specific tax procedure with domestic VAT, reverse charge, and withholding tax types configured — Example: Turkish VAT codes and withholding tax keys set up in FTXP and Extended Withholding Tax.

### ⚙️ CONFIG STEPS
1. **OX15** — define the company, the legal consolidation unit behind one or more company codes · Example: Company CBTR for the Turkish legal entity, kept separate from the German parent company · Where: SPRO ▸ Enterprise Structure ▸ Definition ▸ Financial Accounting
2. **EC01** — copy or create the company-code organizational object from the approved template · Example: Create TR02 from the closest retail/trading template, then replace currency, language, tax and bank localization · Where: SPRO ▸ Enterprise Structure ▸ Definition ▸ Financial Accounting ▸ Edit, Copy, Delete, Check Company Code
3. **OX16 / OX18** — assign the company code to the company and assign each plant to the company code that owns its stock and postings · Example: TR02 receives the Turkish sales/warehouse plants; a German plant is never assigned to the Turkish legal books · Where: SPRO ▸ Enterprise Structure ▸ Assignment ▸ Financial Accounting
4. **OKKP** — maintain the controlling area and assign the company code for cost accounting · Example: One group controlling area with fiscal-year variant K4 and company-code currency control, unless local CO requires a separate area · Where: SPRO ▸ Controlling ▸ General Controlling ▸ Maintain Controlling Area
5. **OBY6** — set company-code global parameters: chart of accounts, fiscal-year variant, posting-period variant, field-status variant and tolerances · Example: TR02 uses the group chart of accounts, local currency TRY and the group fiscal-year variant · Where: SPRO ▸ Financial Accounting Global Settings ▸ Company Code ▸ Enter Global Parameters
6. **FTXP / OB40** — maintain country tax codes and the tax G/L accounts used by purchasing and sales · Example: Turkish domestic input/output VAT, zero-rated export and reverse-charge cases are separate codes, never one blended rate · Where: SPRO ▸ Financial Accounting Global Settings ▸ Tax on Sales/Purchases ▸ Basic Settings ▸ Define Tax Codes for Sales and Purchases
7. **FBZP / F110** — configure payment methods, house-bank determination and the automatic payment run · Example: Local bank, permitted currencies, payment format and approval/release rules are tested with one real vendor payment · Where: SPRO ▸ Financial Accounting ▸ Accounts Payable and Accounts Receivable ▸ Business Transactions ▸ Outgoing Payments
8. **LTMC** — load opening balances, open AP/AR items, assets and inventory through controlled migration objects · Example: Every LTMC load is reconciled to the legacy trial balance and subledger totals before users are released · Where: SAP Migration Cockpit (Fiori app Migrate Your Data / LTMC)
9. **OBYA** — maintain cross-company-code clearing accounts so an intercompany sale in one code and the purchase in the other clear automatically · Example: Delivering code DE01 sells to receiving code TR02: OBYA posts Dr IC customer / Cr IC vendor through the clearing accounts instead of leaving manual balances · Where: SPRO ▸ Financial Accounting ▸ Accounts Receivable and Accounts Payable ▸ Business Transactions ▸ Prepare Cross-Company-Code Transactions
10. **VF01** — create the intercompany billing document (billing type IV) from the cross-company delivery so revenue and the IC receivable are one auditable chain · Example: Cross-company STO: ME21N order, VL10B delivery, goods issue, then VF01 with billing type IV and the IDoc INVOIC posts the vendor invoice on the receiving side · Where: Sales and Distribution ▸ Billing ▸ Billing Processing ▸ Create Billing Document (VF01)
11. **FBICR3** — run intercompany reconciliation so IC receivables and payables match across company codes before close · Example: Month-end IC confirmation: FBICR3 shows zero unmatched documents between the group codes; differences are fixed at source, never plugged · Where: Financial Accounting ▸ General Ledger ▸ Periodic Processing ▸ Intercompany Reconciliation ▸ Execute Intercompany Reconciliation (FBICR3)

### 🔧 DROP THESE OBJECT NAMES
- **OX15** — company definition for consolidation
- **EC01** — company-code copy/create object
- **OKKP** — controlling-area maintenance
- **OBY6** — company-code global parameters
- **FTXP** — country tax-code maintenance
- **FBZP** — payment-program configuration
- **LTMC** — controlled cutover data load
- **OBYA** — cross-company clearing accounts
- **FBICR3** — intercompany reconciliation
- **ACDOCA** — one journal line for every ledger

### 🧾 ACCOUNTING ENTRIES
- Dr Expense / asset / inventory 50,000 / Cr Vendor or bank 50,000 — first local purchase proves tax, plant and account determination.
- Dr Customer 50,000 / Cr Revenue and output tax 50,000 — first local sale proves VKOA, tax code and sales-area assignment.
- Dr Intercompany Clearing DE01 50,000 / Cr Intercompany Revenue DE01 50,000 — cross-company delivery billing (IV).
- Dr Intercompany Expense TR02 50,000 / Cr Intercompany Clearing TR02 50,000 — intercompany vendor invoice posting on receiving side.

### ⚙️ HOW TO TEST IT
1. **OX03 / SE16H** — verify company code configuration and global parameters in table T001.
2. **FB50 / F-02** — post a test general ledger document in the new company code to verify posting periods and document numbering.
3. **MIGO / MIRO** — execute a complete procure-to-pay cycle in the new plant/company code to test OBYC and tax determination.
4. **F.01 / FAGLL03** — run the trial balance report in FAGLL03 and balance sheet in F.01 to prove ACDOCA captures local and group ledger balances correctly.

### 🔗 HOW IT INTEGRATES (FI / MM / SD / PP)
- MM inventory posting (MIGO) → Dr Inventory / Cr GR/IR clearing → inventory cost object → ACDOCA, seen in FAGLL03.
- SD billing document (VF01) → Dr Customer / Cr Revenue and Output Tax → profitability segment (Margin Analysis) → ACDOCA, seen in KE24 / FAGLL03.
- PP settlement (KO88) → Dr Cost of Goods Sold / Cr WIP or Order Settlement → production cost center / order → ACDOCA, seen in KOB1.
- FI payment run (F110) → Dr Vendor / Cr House Bank clearing → payment clearing object → ACDOCA, seen in FBL1N.

### 📅 PERIOD-END CLOSING SEQUENCE
1. **F.5D** — master-data check to verify all cost centers and profit centers are active.
2. **KB15N** — manual cost allocations and repostings for overhead distribution.
3. **AS02 / AFAB** — asset depreciation run for fixed assets in the local depreciation area.
4. **KSSJ** — actual overhead split and plan/actual cost calculation for production orders.
5. **KSII** — actual activity price calculation for manufacturing cost centers.
6. **CO88** — settlement of manufacturing orders to inventory and variance accounts.
7. **F.13** — automatic clearing of open items for clearing accounts and GR/IR.
8. **FBICR3** — intercompany reconciliation to clear discrepancies between group entities.
9. **FAGL_FC_VAL** — foreign currency valuation for open receivables, payables, and bank balances.
10. **F.01** — financial statement generation for local statutory and group reporting.
11. **OB52** — closing posting periods to lock the period against further postings.

### 🩺 TROUBLESHOOTING — CONFIG, MASTER DATA OR TRANSACTION?
- Symptom: Tax code not appearing during MM/SD transaction posting → it is configuration → check FTXP and OBCO → assign the correct tax procedure to the country and company code.
- Symptom: Intercompany billing failing with partner determination error → it is master data → check customer-vendor link in XD03/BP and VD01 → assign the correct customer master to the vendor trading partner.
- Symptom: Balance sheet out of balance during foreign currency valuation → it is configuration → check OB08 and OBYA → maintain correct exchange rate types and valuation accounts.

### 💼 THE BUSINESS STORY I TELL
When rolling out our Turkish operations at CYBEX, our primary challenge was aligning strict local legal requirements with our standardized group IFRS template. I chose to extend our master template by creating a dedicated company code with local currency TRY while preserving the group chart of accounts and parallel ledgers in ACDOCA. I rejected a totally standalone implementation because it would have broken our global consolidation workflows and intercompany automation. Instead, we built out the exact company structure, configured regional tax procedures for domestic and export VAT, and tested the full procure-to-pay and order-to-cash cycles before go-live. We proved the design using end-to-end integration tests covering local invoice posting, bank payments, and intercompany clearing with our German entity. The business successfully went live with fully automated statutory reporting and clean group consolidation from day one.

### 🪤 TRAPS & THE ANSWER THAT WINS
- Trap: Copying a standard company code without checking currency and chart of accounts assignments. → Winning line: "We always review OBY6 global parameters and currency types first to prevent structural data corruption during template rollouts."
- Trap: Assuming local tax procedures can use generic group tax codes without country-specific condition types. → Winning line: "Local statutory tax requirements mandate specific FTXP tax codes and tax jurisdiction structures that must be tested independently before any transactional posting."

### 🎯 IF MY MIND GOES BLANK
- Country setup links company code definition, local currency, tax procedures, and intercompany clearing into the Universal Journal.
- It replaced decentralized regional ledger reconciliation with real-time parallel accounting in ACDOCA.
- Key objects: OX15, OBY6, FTXP, and OBYA.

## 87. Asset accounting

### 💡 SAY THIS FIRST
In my last rollout, asset accounting was driven by New Asset Accounting in S/4HANA, which eliminated delta areas through technical clearing accounts.

### 🗣️ DIRECT ANSWER TO SPEAK NOW
- **Core Concept:** New Asset Accounting values the same asset in parallel by depreciation area and ledger, where the asset class drives account determination and depreciation keys, and postings update the asset subledger in real time.
- **Key System Benefit:** S/4HANA removed the old delta-area workaround for parallel valuations: integrated acquisitions use a technical clearing account so each ledger and area receives the correct value from the original document.
- **Execution Strategy:** The chart of depreciation, depreciation areas, account determination, asset classes, and number ranges must be designed together via OAOB and AO90 so that assets inherit the correct valuation and accounts.

### 📊 ARCHITECTURAL FLOW
```
1. STRUCTURE OAOB · OADB
 chart of depreciation and areas assigned

 ↓
2. MASTER AS01
 asset class creates account and depreciation defaults

 ↓
3. ACQUIRE F-90 · MIRO
 asset value posted by area/ledger

 ↓
4. DEPRECIATE AFAB
 planned depreciation posted

 ↓
5. CLOSE / PROVE AJAB · AW01N
 year close and asset history verified

```

### ⚙️ CONFIG STEPS
1. **OAOB** — assign the chart of depreciation to the company code · Example: Each company code uses the country chart that carries its statutory depreciation areas · Where: SPRO ▸ Financial Accounting ▸ Asset Accounting ▸ Organizational Structures ▸ Assign Chart of Depreciation to Company Code
2. **OADB** — review depreciation areas and their ledger and accounting-principle assignment · Example: Book, IFRS, and local-tax areas value the same asset without duplicate asset masters · Where: SPRO ▸ Financial Accounting ▸ Asset Accounting ▸ Valuation ▸ Depreciation Areas ▸ Specify Depreciation Areas
3. **AO90** — maintain account determination for asset classes and depreciation areas · Example: Acquisition, accumulated depreciation, and gain or loss accounts are separated by asset class · Where: SPRO ▸ Financial Accounting ▸ Asset Accounting ▸ Integration with General Ledger Accounting ▸ Assign General Ledger Accounts
4. **AS01** — create the asset master from the correct asset class · Example: The class defaults useful life, depreciation key, and account determination before the first posting · Where: SAP GUI ▸ Accounting ▸ Financial Accounting ▸ Fixed Assets ▸ Asset ▸ AS01 - Create
5. **AFAB** — execute the depreciation run for the period · Example: Planned depreciation of fifty thousand posts by depreciation area and updates the asset history · Where: SAP GUI ▸ Fixed Assets ▸ Periodic Processing ▸ Depreciation Run ▸ AFAB
6. **AJAB** — close the asset fiscal year after depreciation and reconciliation are complete · Example: No year is closed while unposted depreciation or asset-to-GL differences remain · Where: SAP GUI ▸ Fixed Assets ▸ Periodic Processing ▸ Year-End Closing ▸ AJAB

### 🔧 DROP THESE OBJECT NAMES
- **OAOB** — chart of depreciation assignment
- **OADB** — depreciation-area definition
- **AO90** — asset account determination
- **AS01** — asset master creation
- **AFAB** — depreciation posting run
- **AW01N** — asset history and values
- **AJAB** — asset fiscal-year close

### 🧾 ACCOUNTING ENTRIES
- Dr Fixed asset 50,000 / Cr Technical clearing account 50,000 — integrated acquisition before area-specific valuation is completed.
- Dr Depreciation expense 50,000 / Cr Accumulated depreciation 50,000 — AFAB period posting.
- Dr Accumulated depreciation and loss on disposal 50,000 / Cr Fixed asset 50,000 — retirement removes cost and reserves.
- Dr Asset under construction 50,000 / Cr Vendor or internal activity 50,000 — capital project before settlement to the final asset.

### 🧪 HOW TO TEST IT
1. Open AS01, create an asset, post an acquisition via F-90, and inspect every depreciation area in AW01N.
2. Open AFAB, run depreciation in test mode, correct any account or cost-object error, then post and prove the journal in ACDOCA.
3. Transfer and retire one asset, then reconcile asset history to the GL balances.
4. Run the asset-to-GL reconciliation before AJAB and keep the signed difference list.

### 🪤 TRAPS & THE ANSWER THAT WINS
- Trap: Creating a new asset class for every single asset. → Winning line: Classes group valuation and account rules; masters carry the individual asset.
- Trap: Fixing depreciation only in the leading ledger. → Winning line: Check every depreciation area and its ledger assignment in AW01N.

### 🎯 IF MY MIND GOES BLANK
Asset class drives the rules, AS01 creates the asset, AFAB posts depreciation, and AW01N proves the value by area.

## 88. shut off accounts are there and which is connected to the chart of depreciation

### 💡 SAY THIS FIRST
Account determination in asset accounting links the asset class to general ledger reconciliation accounts via transaction AO90.

### 🗣️ DIRECT ANSWER TO SPEAK NOW
- **Core Concept:** Control accounts in Asset Accounting, often referred to as reconciliation accounts or shut-off accounts, bridge subledger asset values directly to the general ledger.
- **Key System Benefit:** S/4HANA connects the chart of depreciation and account determination directly to the Universal Journal (ACDOCA), ensuring real-time multi-ledger balance integrity without legacy reconciliation gaps.
- **Execution Strategy:** Transaction AO90 links asset classes and depreciation areas to balance sheet and expense accounts, driven by the assigned chart of depreciation in OAOB.

### 📊 ARCHITECTURAL FLOW
```
1. STRUCTURE OAOB · OADB
 chart of depreciation assigned to company code

 ↓
2. CONFIG AO90
 map asset class and areas to G/L reconciliation accounts

 ↓
3. MASTER AS01
 asset class pulls correct account determination automatically

 ↓
4. POSTING F-90 · MIRO
 acquisition posts to subledger and G/L simultaneously

 ↓
5. VERIFICATION AW01N · FBL3N
 prove asset values match reconciliation balances

```

### ⚙️ CONFIG STEPS
1. **OAOB** — assign the chart of depreciation to the company code · Example: Chart 0DE assigned to company code TR02 · Where: SPRO ▸ Financial Accounting ▸ Asset Accounting ▸ Organizational Structures ▸ Assign Chart of Depreciation to Company Code
2. **OADB** — define and review depreciation areas and their accounting principles · Example: Area 01 for book depreciation, Area 15 for IFRS · Where: SPRO ▸ Financial Accounting ▸ Asset Accounting ▸ Valuation ▸ Depreciation Areas
3. **AO90** — maintain account determination for asset classes and depreciation areas · Example: Asset class 1000 linked to acquisition account 160000 and accumulated depreciation 161000 · Where: SPRO ▸ Financial Accounting ▸ Asset Accounting ▸ Integration with General Ledger Accounting ▸ Assign Account Determination
4. **AS01** — create asset master records using the defined asset class · Example: Asset 1000000 created under class 1000, inheriting AO90 rules · Where: SAP GUI ▸ Accounting ▸ Financial Accounting ▸ Fixed Assets ▸ Asset ▸ AS01 - Create
5. **F-90** — post an integrated asset acquisition with vendor · Example: Dr Fixed Asset 120,000 / Cr Vendor 120,000 via technical clearing · Where: SAP GUI ▸ Accounting ▸ Financial Accounting ▸ Fixed Assets ▸ Posting ▸ Acquisition ▸ F-90 - Acquisition from Vendor
6. **AFAB** — execute the periodic depreciation run · Example: Depreciation expense 10,000 posted across designated areas · Where: SAP GUI ▸ Accounting ▸ Financial Accounting ▸ Fixed Assets ▸ Periodic Processing ▸ Depreciation Run ▸ AFAB
7. **AW01N** — inspect asset explorer to verify planned and posted values · Example: Asset 1000000 verified across areas 01 and 15 · Where: SAP GUI ▸ Accounting ▸ Financial Accounting ▸ Fixed Assets ▸ Asset ▸ AW01N - Asset Explorer
8. **AJAB** — close the asset fiscal year after reconciliation · Example: Year closed for company code TR02 after verifying balance parity · Where: SAP GUI ▸ Accounting ▸ Financial Accounting ▸ Fixed Assets ▸ Periodic Processing ▸ Year-End Closing ▸ AJAB

### 🔧 DROP THESE OBJECT NAMES
- **AO90** — asset account determination assignment
- **OAOB** — chart of depreciation assignment
- **OADB** — depreciation area valuation setup
- **AS01** — asset master record creation
- **AW01N** — asset explorer and value tracking
- **AFAB** — periodic depreciation posting run
- **ACDOCA** — universal journal entry table

### 🧾 ACCOUNTING ENTRIES
- Dr Fixed Asset Recon Account 120,000 / Cr Technical Clearing Account 120,000 — integrated acquisition posting from accounts payable
- Dr Depreciation Expense 10,000 / Cr Accumulated Depreciation 10,000 — periodic depreciation run via AFAB
- Dr Accumulated Depreciation 50,000 / Cr Fixed Asset Recon Account 50,000 — asset retirement posting
- Dr Loss on Asset Retirement 5,000 / Cr Fixed Asset Recon Account 5,000 — clearing remaining net book value on retirement

### 🧪 HOW TO TEST IT
1. Open AS01 and create a test asset using the configured asset class linked in AO90.
2. Post an acquisition using F-90 or MIRO against the newly created asset master.
3. Open AW01N to inspect that the asset values update correctly across all active depreciation areas.
4. Run FBL3N for the reconciliation G/L account and confirm it matches the total subledger asset values in ACDOCA.

### 🪤 TRAPS & THE ANSWER THAT WINS
- Trap: Assuming reconciliation accounts can be posted to directly like normal G/L accounts. → Winning line: Reconciliation accounts block direct manual journal entries to preserve subledger integrity.
- Trap: Modifying account determination after asset transactions have already been posted. → Winning line: Changing AO90 assignments post-go-live causes balance discrepancies and requires migration adjustments.

### 🎯 IF MY MIND GOES BLANK
Account determination in AO90 links asset classes to reconciliation accounts, connected through the chart of depreciation assigned via OAOB.

## 90. what is depreciation area and deprecision key

### 💡 SAY THIS FIRST
A depreciation area values an asset for a specific accounting principle, while the depreciation key dictates how that value reduces over time.

### 🗣️ DIRECT ANSWER TO SPEAK NOW
- **Core Concept:** A depreciation area determines how an asset is valued for a specific book or tax purpose, while the depreciation key calculates the periodic depreciation percentage or amount based on useful life and method.
- **Key System Benefit:** S/4HANA ties depreciation areas directly to ledgers in the Universal Journal, replacing the complex delta areas and reconciliation ledgers required in ECC.
- **Execution Strategy:** You configure areas in OADB and keys in AFIN, linking them through the depreciation schedule on the asset class and master record.

### 📊 ARCHITECTURAL FLOW
```
1. AREA OADB
 define valuation and ledger assignment

 ↓
2. KEY AFIN
 assign calculation method and useful life

 ↓
3. CLASS AO90
 link valuation rules to account determination

 ↓
4. MASTER AS01
 depreciation area and key attached to asset

 ↓
5. EXECUTE AFAB
 run depreciation posting to ACDOCA

```

### ⚙️ CONFIG STEPS
1. **OADB** — define depreciation areas and assign them to accounting principles and ledgers · Example: Area 01 for IFRS ledger 0L, Area 15 for local HGB ledger L1 · Where: SPRO ▸ Financial Accounting ▸ Asset Accounting ▸ Valuation ▸ Depreciation Areas ▸ Define Depreciation Areas
2. **AFIN** — maintain depreciation keys for calculation methods and phases · Example: Straight-line 5-year key for IFRS and 6-year key for local tax · Where: SPRO ▸ Financial Accounting ▸ Asset Accounting ▸ Depreciation ▸ Valuation Methods ▸ Depreciation Key ▸ Maintain Depreciation Key
3. **AO90** — maintain account determination for asset classes across areas · Example: Link asset class 1000 to APC account 700000 and depreciation accounts by area · Where: SPRO ▸ Financial Accounting ▸ Asset Accounting ▸ Integration with General Ledger Accounting ▸ Assign General Ledger Accounts
4. **AS01** — create asset master and verify the assigned areas and keys · Example: Machine asset takes over Area 01 (IFRS, 5yr SL) and Area 15 (HGB, 6yr SL) automatically · Where: SAP GUI ▸ Accounting ▸ Financial Accounting ▸ Fixed Assets ▸ Asset ▸ AS01 - Create
5. **AFAB** — execute depreciation run to post planned amounts · Example: Period run posts €1,000 for IFRS and €833.33 for local GAAP simultaneously · Where: SAP GUI ▸ Fixed Assets ▸ Periodic Processing ▸ Depreciation Run ▸ AFAB
6. **AW01N** — inspect asset explorer to verify values per area · Example: Check tab values for Area 01 and Area 15 to confirm parallel depreciation lines · Where: SAP GUI ▸ Accounting ▸ Financial Accounting ▸ Fixed Assets ▸ Asset ▸ AW01N - Asset Explorer

### 🔧 DROP THESE OBJECT NAMES
- **OADB** — defines depreciation area parameters and ledger mapping
- **AFIN** — configures calculation rules for depreciation keys
- **AO90** — maps account determination by depreciation area
- **AS01** — assigns depreciation keys in asset master data
- **AFAB** — executes periodic depreciation posting run
- **AW01N** — displays asset values per depreciation area

### 🧾 ACCOUNTING ENTRIES
- Dr 700000 APC – Machinery 60,000.00 / Cr 160000 Vendor 60,000.00 — asset acquisition posting. (NI01_FICO_Greenfield_Complete_v2-1.pdf)
- Dr 600000 Depreciation Expense 1,000.00 / Cr 750000 Accum Depreciation 1,000.00 — AFAB depreciation month 1 for IFRS ledger 0L. (NI01_FICO_Greenfield_Complete_v2-1.pdf)
- Dr 600000 Depreciation Expense 833.33 / Cr 750000 Accum Depreciation 833.33 — AFAB depreciation month 1 for local HGB ledger L1. (NI01_FICO_Greenfield_Complete_v2-1.pdf)

### 🧪 HOW TO TEST IT
1. Open AS01 and create an asset, verifying that the depreciation key and areas populate from the asset class.
2. Post an acquisition of €60,000 for the asset and open AW01N to review the planned values across all areas.
3. Execute AFAB in test mode for the current period, check for errors, and run it live.
4. Verify the parallel postings in the Universal Journal ACDOCA to ensure both ledger 0L and L1 recorded their correct depreciation amounts.

### 🪤 TRAPS & THE ANSWER THAT WINS
- Trap: Assuming all depreciation areas must post to the General Ledger in real-time. → Winning line: Only the leading area posts live, while secondary areas post periodically via AFAB or use ledger-specific settings.
- Trap: Modifying a standard depreciation key directly without copying. → Winning line: Always copy standard keys to a custom Z-key before adjusting calculation phases or useful life.

### 🎯 IF MY MIND GOES BLANK
A depreciation area holds the valuation for a specific ledger, a depreciation key calculates how that value drops over time, and AFAB posts the result.

## 92. how I set accounting is connected to Copa

### 💡 SAY THIS FIRST
Account-based and costing-based profitability analysis connect directly to your general ledger and billing condition types in S/4HANA.

### 🗣️ DIRECT ANSWER TO SPEAK NOW
- **Core Concept:** CO-PA connects sales and financial accounting so you can see profitability by customer, product, region, or distribution channel.
- **Key System Benefit:** In S/4HANA, account-based margin analysis reads the universal journal ACDOCA directly, ensuring your profitability data reconciles perfectly with your general ledger P&L.
- **Execution Strategy:** You link the operating concern to your controlling area via KEKK, map SD condition types to value fields using KE4I, and activate the setup with KEKE.

### 📊 ARCHITECTURAL FLOW
```
1. OPERATING CONCERN KEA0
 define characteristics and value fields for GB01

 ↓
2. ASSIGNMENT KEKK
 link controlling area to operating concern

 ↓
3. CONDITION MAPPING KE4I
 map pricing condition types to CO-PA value fields

 ↓
4. ACTIVATION KEKE
 activate profitability analysis status 4 for both types

 ↓
5. REPORTING KE24
 display line items in account-based or costing-based view

```

### ⚙️ CONFIG STEPS
1. **KEA0** — define the operating concern: characteristics and value fields · Example: Operating concern GB01 with characteristics like region and customer, plus value fields for revenue and COGS · Where: SPRO ▸ Controlling ▸ Profitability Analysis ▸ Structure
2. **KEKK** — assign the controlling area to the operating concern · Example: Controlling area assigned to operating concern GB01 so billing documents flow through · Where: SPRO ▸ Controlling ▸ Profitability Analysis ▸ Structures
3. **KEBD** — set the operating concern and choose the working mode for KE24 display · Example: Select GB01 and choose either account-based margin analysis or costing-based view · Where: SPRO ▸ Controlling ▸ Profitability Analysis ▸ Tools
4. **KE4I** — assign SD condition types to CO-PA value fields for costing-based profitability · Example: Map list price condition Z001 to revenue value field, and VPRS to cost of goods sold · Where: SPRO ▸ Controlling ▸ Profitability Analysis ▸ Flows of Actual Values
5. **KE4M** — assign SD quantity fields to value fields · Example: Map billing quantity to ABSMG so sales volumes appear alongside financial values · Where: SPRO ▸ Controlling ▸ Profitability Analysis ▸ Flows of Actual Values
6. **KEKE** — activate Profitability Analysis with status 4 for both types · Example: Set status to 4 to activate both account-based and costing-based profitability reporting · Where: SPRO ▸ Controlling ▸ Profitability Analysis ▸ Environments ▸ Activate Profitability Analysis
7. **KER1** — define key figure schemes for reporting calculations · Example: Create scheme 01 where revenue minus COGS equals contribution margin for KE30 reports · Where: SPRO ▸ Controlling ▸ Profitability Analysis ▸ Information System
8. **KE24** — display CO-PA line items and switch between margin analysis and costing-based views · Example: Review posted billing document 90000001 in KE24 to verify both views populate correctly · Where: SAP Easy Access ▸ Controlling ▸ Profitability Analysis ▸ Information System ▸ KE24 - Line Items

### 🔧 DROP THESE OBJECT NAMES
- **KEA0** — operating concern definition transaction
- **KEKK** — controlling area to operating concern assignment
- **KEBD** — operating concern view setting
- **KEKE** — profitability analysis activation status 4
- **KE4I** — SD condition to value field mapping
- **KE4M** — quantity field assignment transaction
- **ACDOCA** — universal journal table for account-based CO-PA
- **KE24** — profitability analysis line item display

### 🧾 ACCOUNTING ENTRIES
- Goods issue (VL02N): Dr COGS 5111000000 EUR 150.00 / Cr Inventory EUR 150.00 — posted upon delivery completion.
- Billing (VF01): Dr Customer EUR 352.44 / Cr Sales 4111000000 EUR 346.40 / Cr Output Tax EUR 56.27 — recorded during customer invoice creation.
- Promo discount (VF01): Dr Discounts 4411000000 EUR 50.23 / Cr Customer EUR 50.23 — applied during billing document pricing.
- Account-based CO-PA: Dr P&L accounts in ACDOCA read directly by margin analysis — triggered in real-time during billing posting.
- Costing-based CO-PA: Posted to value fields via KE4I condition mapping — triggered simultaneously with billing document release.

### 🧪 HOW TO TEST IT
1. **KEA0** — open KEA0 and verify that operating concern GB01 is active and contains the required characteristics and value fields.
2. **VF01** — create a sales billing document with pricing conditions and save it to generate accounting and profitability documents.
3. **KE24** — open KE24, enter operating concern GB01, and inspect the line item display in both account-based and costing-based views.
4. **FAGLL03H** — run the general ledger line item browser for the revenue and COGS accounts to reconcile totals against account-based profitability results.

### 🪤 TRAPS & THE ANSWER THAT WINS
- Trap: Assuming account-based CO-PA requires manual condition mapping like costing-based CO-PA does → Winning line: Account-based margin analysis reads the G/L accounts and universal journal directly without needing KE4I mapping.
- Trap: Activating profitability analysis after posting historical billing documents → Winning line: Documents posted before activation via KEKE will never appear in CO-PA, so activation must happen during cutover.

### 🎯 IF MY MIND GOES BLANK
Profitability analysis connects sales billing and general ledger accounts to operating concerns using KEA0 and KEKK. It replaced separate legacy CO-PA summary tables with Universal Journal integration in S/4HANA. Use transaction KE24 to verify your postings.

## 95. how does S4 Hannah handle an impairment posted only two Ledger zero l when calculating here three straight line the precision after a total useful life extension from 10 to 12 years

### 💡 SAY THIS FIRST
S/4HANA handles impairment and useful life extensions in Asset Accounting by recalculating planned depreciation across remaining periods in the affected ledger's depreciation area.

### 🗣️ DIRECT ANSWER TO SPEAK NOW
- **Core Concept:** An impairment posted to ledger zero (Area 01) reduces the net book value, while the useful life extension from 10 to 12 years recalculates the remaining planned depreciation over the new horizon without altering historical periods.
- **Key System Benefit:** S/4HANA Asset Accounting uses depreciation areas assigned to parallel ledgers in the Universal Journal (ACDOCA), ensuring the impairment and revised depreciation schedule post exclusively to the target ledger without corrupting local GAAP books.
- **Execution Strategy:** The depreciation key must be configured with a calculation method that dynamically spreads the remaining net book value over the newly extended useful life, executed via AS02 master data change and AFAB depreciation run.

### 📊 ARCHITECTURAL FLOW
```
1. MASTER AS02
 extend useful life from 10 to 12 years in asset master

 ↓

2. IMPAIRMENT ABAA
 post impairment explicitly to ledger zero / depreciation area 01

3. RECALCULATION AFAB (Test Run)
 system recalculates remaining NBV over new useful life

4. DEPRECIATION AFAB (Productive)
 post adjusted monthly depreciation to ACDOCA ledger zero

### ⚙️ CONFIG STEPS
1. **AS02** — modify the asset master record to extend the useful life from 10 to 12 years · Example: Asset 1000/123456 life changed from 120 to 144 periods · Where: SAP GUI ▸ Accounting ▸ Financial Accounting ▸ Fixed Assets ▸ Asset ▸ Change
2. **ABAA** — post manual impairment directly to the specific depreciation area for ledger zero · Example: Impairment of USD 12,000 posted to Area 01 (Leading Ledger) · Where: SAP GUI ▸ Fixed Assets ▸ Periodic Processing ▸ Year-End Closing ▸ Post Depreciation
3. **OAYR** — check fiscal year control and allow depreciation recalculation for open periods · Example: Ensure posting periods remain open for retroactive or prospective recalculation · Where: SPRO ▸ Financial Accounting ▸ Asset Accounting ▸ Financial Years
4. **AFAB** — execute the depreciation run to recalculate and post the new planned values · Example: Remaining NBV of USD 60,000 spread over remaining 60 months yielding USD 1,000 monthly depreciation · Where: SAP GUI ▸ Fixed Assets ▸ Periodic Processing ▸ Depreciation Run

### 🔧 DROP THESE OBJECT NAMES
- **ACDOCA** — Universal Journal line items table storing asset postings
- **AS02** — asset master change transaction for useful life
- **ABAA** — manual depreciation and impairment posting transaction
- **AFAB** — periodic depreciation posting run transaction
- **AW01N** — asset explorer for viewing values by depreciation area
- **ANLC** — asset value fields table for parallel currencies and ledgers

### 🧾 ACCOUNTING ENTRIES
- Dr Impairment loss (P&L) 12,000 / Cr Accumulated impairment (Balance Sheet) 12,000 — when ABAA posts the ledger-zero impairment.
- Dr Depreciation expense 1,000 / Cr Accumulated depreciation 1,000 — when AFAB posts the recalculated monthly straight-line depreciation over the extended life.

### 🧪 HOW TO TEST IT
1. Open AW01N for the test asset to inspect initial planned depreciation and useful life of 10 years (120 periods).
2. Post the impairment using ABAA to ledger zero and verify the net book value reduction in the leading depreciation area.
3. Update the asset master in AS02, changing useful life to 12 years (144 periods), and check AW01N to confirm the remaining depreciation curve flattens over the new horizon.
4. Run AFAB for the period and verify the resulting posting in ACDOCA matches the new monthly calculation.

### 🪤 TRAPS & THE ANSWER THAT WINS
- Trap: Assuming the system automatically recalculates historical closed periods when useful life is extended. → Winning line: Prospective changes only affect remaining open periods in the depreciation schedule, leaving past posted periods untouched.
- Trap: Posting the impairment to all depreciation areas when the requirement specifies ledger zero only. → Winning line: Select the specific depreciation area corresponding to ledger zero during the ABAA posting so parallel ledgers remain unaffected.

DIRECT ANSWER TO SPEAK NOW
> In S/4HANA, asset impairments and depreciation calculations are handled in the Universal Journal (ACDOCA) across parallel ledgers. When an impairment is posted only to leading ledger 0L (or a specific ledger group via accounting principles) and a useful life extension occurs (e.g., from 10 to 12 years), the system recalculates straight-line depreciation prospectively over the remaining useful life based on the new Net Book Value (NBV) minus the impairment, ensuring ledger-specific valuation differences are maintained in ACDOCA.

ARCHITECTURAL FLOW
```
[Asset Transaction / Impairment] --> Posted via AB01L / AS02 to Ledger 0L (or specific Accounting Principle)
 |
 +-- Updates ACDOCA (Universal Journal) with RBUKRS, GJAHR, BELNR, RACCT, PRCTR, HSLVT
 |
 +-- AFAB (Depreciation Run) reads APC, Accumulated Depreciation, Impairment, and Useful Life
 |
 +-- Calculates prospective straight-line depreciation over remaining useful life (12 years total)
```

CONFIG STEPS (every step with its t-object)
1. Define Chart of Depreciation (`OA84` / `SPRO` -> Financial Accounting -> Asset Accounting -> Organizational Structures -> Copy Chart of Depreciation)
2. Specify Depreciation Areas (`OAYZ` / `SPRO` -> Valuation -> Depreciation Areas)
3. Assign Chart of Depreciation to Company Code (`OAOB`)
4. Define Asset Classes (`OAOA`)
5. Determine Depreciation Areas in the Asset Class (`OAYZ`)
6. Define Ledger for General Ledger Accounting (`FINSC_LEDGER` / SPRO -> Financial Accounting -> Financial Accounting Global Settings -> Ledgers -> Ledger)
7. Define Accounting Principles (`SPRO` -> Financial Accounting -> Financial Accounting Global Settings -> Ledgers -> Parallel Accounting -> Define Accounting Principles)
8. Assign Accounting Principle to Ledger Group (`SPRO` -> Parallel Accounting -> Assign Accounting Principle to Ledger Group)

DROP THESE OBJECT NAMES
- OB72 (this is for exchanging company codes / trading partners or similar non-ledger config; ledger groups are configured via transaction `SPRO` under Ledger path, not OB72)
- KALC (ECC FI-CO reconciliation table/t-code; eliminated in S/4HANA Universal Journal)
- BSEG, BSIS, BSAK, GLT0, FAGLFLEXT, COEP (replaced by ACDOCA in S/4HANA)

ACCOUNTING ENTRIES (with numbers)
Let's use a consistent numeric example:
- Initial Acquisition Cost (APC): 120,000
- Initial Useful Life: 10 years (120 periods)
- Initial Annual Depreciation = 120,000 / 10 = 12,000 per year (1,000 per month)
- After 3 years (36 months), Accumulated Depreciation = 3 * 12,000 = 36,000
- Net Book Value (NBV) before impairment = 120,000 - 36,000 = 84,000
- Impairment posted exclusively to Ledger 0L at month 36: 24,000
 - Dr. Impairment Expense (P&L) 24,000
 - Cr. Accumulated Impairment / Asset (BS) 24,000
- Adjusted NBV after Impairment = 84,000 - 24,000 = 60,000
- Useful life extension: Extended from 10 years to 12 years total (144 months total).
- Remaining useful life at month 36 = 144 - 36 = 108 months (9 years).
- New Monthly Depreciation = Adjusted NBV / Remaining Useful Life = 60,000 / 9 years = 6,666.67 per year (555.56 per month).

HOW TO TEST IT
1. Create an asset using AS01 under Company Code 1000 with an initial useful life of 10 years and APC of 120,000.
2. Run periodic depreciation using `AFAB` for the first 36 months to establish the 36,000 accumulated depreciation and 84,000 NBV.
3. Post an impairment of 24,000 specifically to ledger 0L using `AB01L` (Asset Posting with Ledger/Accounting Principle selection).
4. Modify the asset master (`AS02`) to extend the total useful life from 10 to 12 years.
5. Execute `AFAB` for subsequent periods and verify via `ACDOCA` table display that monthly depreciation is correctly recalculated as 60,000 / 9 years = 6,666.67 per year (555.56 per month) for ledger 0L, while parallel ledgers remain unaffected if no delta impairment was posted there.

TRAPS
- Assuming depreciation recalculates retrospectively instead of prospectively; SAP standard rule for useful life extension and impairments is prospective depreciation over the remaining useful life.
- Forgetting that posting impairments via `AB01L` requires proper ledger-group assignment; posting without specifying the accounting principle/ledger group will default to all applicable ledgers.
- Confusing extension ledgers with non-leading full ledgers when dealing with parallel valuation principles (impairments for local GAAP vs IFRS typically require full non-leading ledgers or valuation areas, not mere delta extension ledgers, depending on asset accounting requirements).

IF MY MIND GOES BLANK
> "When asset impairment and useful life changes happen across parallel ledgers in S/4HANA, the Universal Journal (`ACDOCA`) handles the ledger-specific values. I post the impairment via `AB01L` to the specific ledger/accounting principle, update the useful life extension in `AS02`, and let the depreciation run (`AFAB`) calculate prospective straight-line depreciation using the formula: New Depreciation = (NBV - Impairment) / Remaining Useful Life."

### 🎯 IF MY MIND GOES BLANK
Useful life extension changes the remaining denominator in AS02, impairment reduces the numerator via ABAA, and AFAB recalculates the monthly straight-line depreciation for ACDOCA.
